This exercise is a multiple-choice questionnaire. For each of the following questions, exactly one of the four proposed answers is correct. No justification is required.

Let $f$ be the function defined for every real number $x$ in the interval $(0,+\infty)$ by
$$f(x)=\frac{e^{2x}}{x}.$$
The second derivative $f''$ of $f$, defined on the interval $(0,+\infty)$, is given by
$$f''(x)=\frac{2e^{2x}\left(2x^2-2x+1\right)}{x^3}.$$

1. The function $f'$, the derivative of $f$, is defined on the interval $(0,+\infty)$ by:
(a) $f'(x)=2e^{2x}$
(b) $f'(x)=\dfrac{e^{2x}(x-1)}{x^2}$
(c) $f'(x)=\dfrac{e^{2x}(2x-1)}{x^2}$
(d) $f'(x)=\dfrac{e^{2x}(1+2x)}{x^2}$.

2. The function $f$:
(a) is decreasing on $(0,+\infty)$
(b) is monotonic on $(0,+\infty)$
(c) has a minimum at $\frac{1}{2}$
(d) has a maximum at $\frac{1}{2}$.

3. The limit of the function $f$ at $+\infty$ is:
(a) $+\infty$
(b) $0$
(c) $1$
(d) $e^{2x}$.

4. The function $f$:
(a) is concave on $(0,+\infty)$
(b) is convex on $(0,+\infty)$
(c) is concave on $\left(0,\frac{1}{2}\right]$
(d) is represented by a curve that has an inflection point.

A production line manufactures mechanical parts. It is estimated that $5\,\%$ of the parts produced by this line are defective.
An engineer has developed a test to be applied to the parts. This test has two possible results: "positive" or "negative".
The test is applied to a part chosen at random from the production of the line.
We denote by $p(E)$ the probability of an event $E$.
Consider the following events:
• $D$: "the part is defective";
• $T$: "the part has a positive test";
• $\overline{D}$ and $\overline{T}$ denote the complementary events of $D$ and $T$ respectively.
Given the characteristics of the test, we know that:
• the probability that a part has a positive test given that it is defective is equal to $0.98$;
• the probability that a part has a negative test given that it is not defective is equal to $0.97$.

Parts I and II can be treated independently.

Part I
1. Represent the situation by a weighted tree.
2.a. Determine the probability that a part chosen at random from the production of the line is defective and has a positive test.
2.b. Prove that $p(T)=0.0775$.
3. The positive predictive value of the test is the probability that a part is defective given that the test is positive. A test is considered effective if its positive predictive value is greater than $0.95$.
Calculate the positive predictive value of this test and state whether it is effective.

Part II
A sample of 20 parts is chosen from the production of the line, this choice being treated as drawing with replacement. Let $X$ be the random variable giving the number of defective parts in this sample.
Recall that $p(D)=0.05$.
1. Justify that $X$ follows a binomial distribution and determine the parameters of this distribution.
2. Calculate the probability that this sample contains at least one defective part. Give the result rounded to the nearest hundredth.
3. Calculate the expectation of the random variable $X$ and interpret the result obtained.

Cécile has invited friends to lunch on her terrace. For dessert she has planned an assortment of individual cakes that she bought frozen.
She takes the cakes out of the freezer at $-19\,^{\circ}\mathrm{C}$ and brings them to the terrace, where the temperature is $25\,^{\circ}\mathrm{C}$.
After 10 minutes the temperature of the cakes is $1.3\,^{\circ}\mathrm{C}$.

I – First model
Assume that the thawing speed is constant, that is, the increase in temperature is the same minute after minute.
According to this model, determine what the temperature of the cakes would be 25 minutes after they were taken out of the freezer.
Does this model seem relevant?

II – Second model
Let $T_n$ be the temperature of the cakes, in degrees Celsius, $n$ minutes after they were taken out of the freezer; thus $T_0=-19$.
We accept that, to model the evolution of the temperature, the following relation must hold:
$$\text{for every natural number } n,\quad T_{n+1}-T_n=-0.06\times\left(T_n-25\right).$$
1. Justify that, for every integer $n$, $T_{n+1}=0.94T_n+1.5$.
2. Calculate $T_1$ and $T_2$. Give values rounded to the nearest tenth.
3. Prove by induction that, for every natural number $n$, $T_n\leqslant 25$.
Going back to the situation studied, was this result predictable?
4. Study the monotonicity of the sequence $(T_n)$.
5. Prove that the sequence $(T_n)$ is convergent.
6. For every natural number $n$, let $U_n=T_n-25$.
6.a. Show that the sequence $(U_n)$ is a geometric sequence, and give its common ratio and its first term $U_0$.
6.b. Deduce that, for every natural number $n$, $T_n=-44\times 0.94^n+25$.
6.c. Deduce the limit of the sequence $(T_n)$. Interpret this result in the context of the situation studied.
7.a. The manufacturer advises eating the cakes after half an hour at room temperature after taking them out of the freezer.
What temperature have the cakes then reached? Give the value rounded to the nearest integer.
7.b. Cécile is used to these cakes, which she likes to eat while they are still cool, at a temperature of $10\,^{\circ}\mathrm{C}$. Give a bound, between two consecutive integers, of the time in minutes after which Cécile should eat her cake.
7.c. The following program, written in Python, must return after execution the smallest value of the integer $n$ for which $T_n\geqslant 10$.
$$\begin{array}{l}\text{def seuil():}\\ \quad\text{n=0}\\ \quad\text{T= ..........}\\ \quad\text{while T ..........}\\ \quad\quad\text{T= ..........}\\ \quad\quad\text{n=n+1}\\ \quad\text{return}\end{array}$$
Copy this program onto your answer sheet and complete the incomplete lines so that the program returns the expected value.

Main topics: geometry of space with an orthonormal coordinate system; orthogonality in space.

In an orthonormal coordinate system $\left(O;\overrightarrow{i},\overrightarrow{j},\overrightarrow{k}\right)$ consider
• the point A with coordinates $(1,3,2)$,
• the vector $\overrightarrow{u}$ with coordinates $\begin{pmatrix}1\\1\\0\end{pmatrix}$,
• the line $d$ passing through the origin O of the coordinate system and having direction vector $\overrightarrow{u}$.
The aim of this exercise is to determine the point of $d$ closest to the point A and to study some properties of this point.
The figure may be used to support the reasoning throughout the questions.

1. Determine a parametric representation of the line $d$.
2. Let $t$ be any real number, and $M$ the point of the line $d$ with coordinates $(t,t,0)$.
2.a. Let $AM$ denote the distance between the points A and $M$. Prove that
$$AM^2=2t^2-8t+14.$$
2.b. Prove that the point $M_0$ with coordinates $(2,2,0)$ is the point of the line $d$ for which the distance $AM$ is minimal.
You may assume that the distance $AM$ is minimal when its square $AM^2$ is minimal.
3. Prove that the lines $(AM_0)$ and $d$ are orthogonal.
4. Let $A'$ be the orthogonal projection of the point $A$ onto the plane with Cartesian equation $z=0$. The point $A'$ therefore has coordinates $(1,3,0)$.
Prove that the point $M_0$ is the point of the plane $(AA'M_0)$ closest to the point O, the origin of the coordinate system.
5. Calculate the volume of the pyramid $OM_0A'A$.
Recall that the volume of a pyramid is given by $V=\frac{1}{3}\mathcal{B}h$, where $\mathcal{B}$ is the area of a base and $h$ is the height of the pyramid corresponding to this base.

Main topics: differential equations; exponential function.

Consider the differential equation
$$(E)\qquad y'=y+2xe^x.$$
We seek the set of functions defined and differentiable on the set $\mathbb{R}$ of real numbers that are solutions of this equation.
1. Let $u$ be the function defined on $\mathbb{R}$ by $u(x)=x^2e^x$. We accept that $u$ is differentiable and denote by $u'$ its derivative. Prove that $u$ is a particular solution of $(E)$.
2. Let $f$ be a function defined and differentiable on $\mathbb{R}$. Let $g$ be the function defined on $\mathbb{R}$ by
$$g(x)=f(x)-u(x).$$
2.a. Prove that if the function $f$ is a solution of the differential equation $(E)$, then the function $g$ is a solution of the differential equation $y'=y$.
We accept that the converse of this property is also true.
2.b. Using the solution of the differential equation $y'=y$, solve the differential equation $(E)$.
3. Study of the function $u$
3.a. Study the sign of $u'(x)$ for $x$ ranging over $\mathbb{R}$.
3.b. Draw up the table of variations of the function $u$ on $\mathbb{R}$ (the limits are not required).
3.c. Determine the largest interval on which the function $u$ is concave.

This exercise is a multiple-choice questionnaire. For each of the following questions, exactly one of the four proposed answers is correct. No justification is required.

Space is equipped with an orthonormal coordinate system $\left(O;\overrightarrow{i},\overrightarrow{j},\overrightarrow{k}\right)$.
Consider:
• the line $\mathcal{D}$ passing through the points $A(1,1,-2)$ and $B(-1,3,2)$;
• the line $\mathcal{D}'$ with parametric representation
$$\left\{\begin{array}{rcl}x&=&-4+3t\\ y&=&6-3t\\ z&=&8-6t\end{array}\right.\quad\text{with } t\in\mathbb{R};$$
• the plane $\mathcal{P}$ with Cartesian equation $x+my-2z+8=0$, where $m$ is a real number.

Question 1: Which of the following points belongs to the line $\mathcal{D}'$?
(a) $M_1(-1,3,-2)$
(b) $M_2(11,-9,-22)$
(c) $M_3(-7,9,2)$
(d) $M_4(-2,3,4)$

Question 2: A direction vector of the line $\mathcal{D}'$ is:
(a) $\overrightarrow{u_1}\begin{pmatrix}-4\\6\\8\end{pmatrix}$
(b) $\overrightarrow{u_2}\begin{pmatrix}3\\3\\6\end{pmatrix}$
(c) $\overrightarrow{u_3}\begin{pmatrix}3\\-3\\-6\end{pmatrix}$
(d) $\overrightarrow{u_4}\begin{pmatrix}-1\\3\\2\end{pmatrix}$

Question 3: The lines $\mathcal{D}$ and $\mathcal{D}'$ are:
(a) intersecting
(b) strictly parallel
(c) not coplanar
(d) coincident

Question 4: The value of the real number $m$ for which the line $\mathcal{D}$ is parallel to the plane $\mathcal{P}$ is:
(a) $m=-1$
(b) $m=1$
(c) $m=5$
(d) $m=-2$

In this exercise, the requested probabilities are to be rounded to the nearest thousandth if necessary.
Feline leukaemia is a disease affecting cats; it is caused by a virus.
In a large veterinary centre, the proportion of cats carrying the disease is estimated at $40\,\%$.
A screening test for the disease is carried out among the cats present in this veterinary centre.
This test has the following characteristics:
• when the cat carries the disease, its test is positive in $90\,\%$ of cases;
• when the cat does not carry the disease, its test is negative in $85\,\%$ of cases.
A cat is chosen at random in the veterinary centre and the following events are considered:
• $M$: "the cat carries the disease";
• $T$: "the cat's test is positive";
• $\overline{M}$ and $\overline{T}$ denote the complementary events of $M$ and $T$ respectively.

1.a. Represent the situation by a weighted tree.
1.b. Calculate the probability that the cat carries the disease and that its test is positive.
1.c. Show that the probability that the cat's test is positive is equal to $0.45$.
1.d. A cat is chosen among those whose test is positive. Calculate the probability that it carries the disease.
2. A sample of 20 cats is chosen at random in the veterinary centre. We accept that this choice can be treated as drawing with replacement.
Let $X$ be the random variable giving the number of cats with a positive test in the chosen sample.
2.a. Determine, with justification, the distribution of the random variable $X$.
2.b. Calculate the probability that there are exactly 5 cats with a positive test in the sample.
2.c. Calculate the probability that there are at most 8 cats with a positive test in the sample.
2.d. Determine the expectation of the random variable $X$ and interpret the result in the context of the exercise.
3. In this question, a sample of $n$ cats is chosen in the centre, again treated as drawing with replacement. Let $p_n$ be the probability that there is at least one cat with a positive test in this sample.
3.a. Show that $p_n=1-0.55^n$.
3.b. Describe the role of the following program, written in Python, in which the variable $n$ is a natural number and the variable $P$ a real number.
$$\begin{array}{l}\text{def seuil():}\\ \quad n=0\\ \quad P=0\\ \quad\text{while } P<0.99:\\ \quad\quad n=n+1\\ \quad\quad P=1-0.55**n\\ \quad\text{return } n\end{array}$$
3.c. Determine, stating the method used, the value returned by this program.

Consider the sequence $(u_n)$ defined by $u_0=1$ and, for every natural number $n$,
$$u_{n+1}=\frac{4u_n}{u_n+4}.$$
1. The following spreadsheet screenshot shows the values of the terms of the sequence $(u_n)$ for $n$ from 0 to 12, as well as those of the quotient $\dfrac{4}{u_n}$ (the values of $u_n$ being displayed with two decimal digits).
$$\begin{array}{|c|c|c|}\hline n&u_n&\dfrac{4}{u_n}\\ \hline 0&1.00&4\\ \hline 1&0.80&5\\ \hline 2&0.67&6\\ \hline 3&0.57&7\\ \hline 4&0.50&8\\ \hline 5&0.44&9\\ \hline 6&0.40&10\\ \hline 7&0.36&11\\ \hline 8&0.33&12\\ \hline 9&0.31&13\\ \hline 10&0.29&14\\ \hline 11&0.27&15\\ \hline 12&0.25&16\\ \hline\end{array}$$
Using these values, conjecture an expression of $\dfrac{4}{u_n}$ in terms of $n$.
The aim of this exercise is to prove this conjecture (question 5.) and to deduce the limit of the sequence $(u_n)$ (question 6.).
2. Prove by induction that, for every natural number $n$, $u_n>0$.
3. Prove that the sequence $(u_n)$ is decreasing.
4. What can be concluded from questions 2. and 3. about the sequence $(u_n)$?
5. Consider the sequence $(v_n)$ defined for every natural number $n$ by $v_n=\dfrac{4}{u_n}$.
Prove that $(v_n)$ is an arithmetic sequence.
Give its common difference and its first term.
Deduce, for every natural number $n$, the expression of $v_n$ in terms of $n$.
6. Determine, for every natural number $n$, the expression of $u_n$ in terms of $n$.
Deduce the limit of the sequence $(u_n)$.

Main topics: logarithm function; differentiation.

Part 1
Let $h$ be the function defined on the interval $(0,+\infty)$ by
$$h(x)=1+\frac{\ln(x)}{x^2}.$$
We accept that the function $h$ is differentiable on $(0,+\infty)$ and denote by $h'$ its derivative.
1. Determine the limits of $h$ at $0$ and at $+\infty$.
2. Show that, for every real number $x$ in $(0,+\infty)$, $h'(x)=\dfrac{1-2\ln(x)}{x^3}$.
3. Deduce the variations of the function $h$ on the interval $(0,+\infty)$.
4. Show that the equation $h(x)=0$ has a unique solution $\alpha$ in $(0,+\infty)$ and check that $\dfrac{1}{2}<\alpha<1$.
5. Determine the sign of $h(x)$ for $x$ in $(0,+\infty)$.

Part 2
Let $f_1$ and $f_2$ be the functions defined on $(0,+\infty)$ by
$$f_1(x)=x-1-\frac{\ln(x)}{x^2}\quad\text{and}\quad f_2(x)=x-2-\frac{2\ln(x)}{x^2}.$$
Let $\mathcal{C}_1$ and $\mathcal{C}_2$ be the graphs of $f_1$ and $f_2$ respectively in a coordinate system $\left(O;\overrightarrow{i},\overrightarrow{j}\right)$.
1. Show that, for every real number $x$ in $(0,+\infty)$,
$$f_1(x)-f_2(x)=h(x).$$
2. Deduce from the results of Part 1 the relative position of the curves $\mathcal{C}_1$ and $\mathcal{C}_2$.
Justify that their unique intersection point has coordinates $(\alpha,\alpha)$.
Recall that $\alpha$ is the unique solution of the equation $h(x)=0$.

Main topics: exponential function; differentiation; convexity.

Part 1
The figure shows, in the plane equipped with an orthonormal coordinate system, the curve representing the derivative $f'$ of a function $f$ differentiable on $\mathbb{R}$ (the curve shown is that of the derivative $f'$ of the function $f$).
Using this curve, conjecture, justifying your answers:
1. the monotonicity of the function $f$ on $\mathbb{R}$;
2. the convexity of the function $f$ on $\mathbb{R}$.

Part 2
We accept that the function $f$ mentioned in Part 1 is defined on $\mathbb{R}$ by
$$f(x)=(x+2)e^{-x}.$$
Let $\mathcal{C}$ be the graph of $f$ in an orthonormal coordinate system $\left(O;\overrightarrow{i},\overrightarrow{j}\right)$.
We accept that the function $f$ is twice differentiable on $\mathbb{R}$, and denote by $f'$ and $f''$ its first and second derivatives respectively.
1. Show that, for every real number $x$,
$$f(x)=\frac{x}{e^x}+2e^{-x}.$$
Deduce the limit of $f$ at $+\infty$.
Justify that the curve $\mathcal{C}$ has an asymptote, which you will specify.
We accept that $\displaystyle\lim_{x\to-\infty}f(x)=-\infty$.
2.a. Show that, for every real number $x$, $f'(x)=(-x-1)e^{-x}$.
2.b. Study the variations of the function $f$ on $\mathbb{R}$ and draw up its table of variations.
2.c. Show that the equation $f(x)=2$ has a unique solution $\alpha$ on the interval $[-2,-1]$ and give an approximate value of it to within $10^{-1}$.
3. Determine, for every real number $x$, the expression of $f''(x)$ and study the convexity of the function $f$.
What does the point A of the curve $\mathcal{C}$ with abscissa 0 represent for this curve?

This is a multiple-choice questionnaire. For each question, exactly one of the four statements is correct. No justification is required.

1. Consider the function defined on $\mathbb{R}$ by
$$f(x)=xe^{-2x}.$$
Let $f''$ denote the second derivative of the function $f$.
For every real number $x$, $f''(x)$ is equal to:
(a) $(1-2x)e^{-2x}$
(b) $4(x-1)e^{-2x}$
(c) $4e^{-2x}$
(d) $(x+2)e^{-2x}$

2. A student in the penultimate year of the general upper-secondary track chooses three speciality subjects out of the twelve offered.
The number of possible combinations is:
(a) $1728$
(b) $1320$
(c) $220$
(d) $33$

3. The figure shows the graph of $f'$, the derivative of a function $f$ defined on $[0,7]$.
The table of variations of $f$ on the interval $[0,7]$ is:
(a) $\begin{array}{c|ccccc}x&0&&3.25&&7\\ \hline f(x)&&\nearrow&&\searrow&\end{array}$
(b) $\begin{array}{c|ccccccc}x&0&&2&&5&&7\\ \hline f(x)&&\searrow&&\nearrow&&\searrow&\end{array}$
(c) $\begin{array}{c|ccccccc}x&0&&2&&5&&7\\ \hline f(x)&&\nearrow&&\searrow&&\nearrow&\end{array}$
(d) $\begin{array}{c|ccccc}x&0&&2&&7\\ \hline f(x)&&\nearrow&&\searrow&\end{array}$

4. A company manufactures smart cards. Each chip can have two defects, denoted A and B.
A statistical study shows that $2.8\,\%$ of the chips have defect A, $2.2\,\%$ of the chips have defect B and, fortunately, $95.4\,\%$ of the chips have neither of the two defects.
The probability that a chip taken at random has both defects is:
(a) $0.05$
(b) $0.004$
(c) $0.046$
(d) It cannot be determined

5. Let $f$ be a function, assumed differentiable on $\mathbb{R}$, and let $f'$ be its derivative.
The table of variations of $f$ is:
$$\begin{array}{c|ccccc}x&-\infty&&-1&&+\infty\\ \hline &&&0&&\\ f(x)&&\nearrow&&\searrow&\\ &-\infty&&&&-\infty\end{array}$$
According to this table of variations:
(a) $f'$ is positive on $\mathbb{R}$.
(b) $f'$ is positive on $(-\infty,-1]$.
(c) $f'$ is negative on $\mathbb{R}$.
(d) $f'$ is positive on $[-1,+\infty)$.

Throughout this exercise, probabilities are to be rounded, if necessary, to $10^{-3}$.
According to a study, regular users of public transport represent $17\,\%$ of the French population.
Among these regular users, $32\,\%$ are young people aged 18 to 24. (Source: TNS-Sofres)

Part A
A person is interviewed at random and we denote:
• $R$ the event: "the person interviewed regularly uses public transport";
• $J$ the event: "the person interviewed is aged 18 to 24".
1. Represent the situation with a weighted tree (first level: $R$, $\overline{R}$; second level: $J$, $\overline{J}$), which you will copy onto your answer sheet, entering the data of the statement.
2. Calculate the probability $P(R\cap J)$.
3. According to the same study, young people aged 18 to 24 represent $11\,\%$ of the French population.
Show that the probability that the person interviewed is a young person aged 18 to 24 who does not regularly use public transport is $0.056$ to within $10^{-3}$.
4. Deduce the proportion of young people aged 18 to 24 among the non-regular users of public transport.

Part B
During a census of the French population, a census taker interviews 50 people at random in one day about their use of public transport.
The French population is large enough for this census to be treated as drawing with replacement.
Let $X$ be the random variable counting the people who regularly use public transport among the 50 people interviewed.
1. Determine, with justification, the distribution of $X$ and give its parameters.
2. Calculate $P(X=5)$ and interpret the result.
3. The census taker states that there is more than a $95\,\%$ chance that, among the 50 people interviewed, fewer than 13 of them regularly use public transport.
Is this statement true? Justify your answer.
4. What is the mean number of people regularly using public transport among the 50 people interviewed?

In May 2020, a company decides to develop teleworking in order to adopt an environmentally responsible approach.
It then offers its 5000 employees in France the choice between teleworking and working on the company's premises.
In May 2020, only 200 of them chose teleworking.
Every month since this measure was introduced, the company's managers observe that $85\,\%$ of those who had chosen teleworking the previous month choose to continue, and that, each month, 450 additional employees choose teleworking.
The number of employees of this company who telework is modelled by the sequence $(a_n)$.
The term $a_n$ thus denotes an estimate of the number of employees teleworking in the $n$-th month after May 2020. Thus $a_0=200$.

Part A
1. Calculate $a_1$.
2. Justify that for every natural number $n$, $a_{n+1}=0.85a_n+450$.
3. Consider the sequence $(v_n)$ defined for every natural number $n$ by $v_n=a_n-3000$.
3.a. Prove that the sequence $(v_n)$ is a geometric sequence with common ratio $0.85$.
3.b. Express $v_n$ in terms of $n$ for every natural number $n$.
3.c. Deduce that, for every natural number $n$, $a_n=-2800\times 0.85^n+3000$.
4. Determine the number of months after which the number of teleworkers will be strictly greater than 2500, after the introduction of this measure in the company.

Part B
In order to evaluate the impact of this measure on its staff, the company's managers have succeeded in modelling the number of employees satisfied with this scheme by the sequence $(u_n)$ defined by $u_0=1$ and, for every natural number $n$,
$$u_{n+1}=\frac{5u_n+4}{u_n+2},$$
where $u_n$ denotes the number of thousands of employees satisfied with this new measure $n$ months after May 2020.
1. Prove that the function $f$ defined for every $x\in[0,+\infty)$ by $f(x)=\dfrac{5x+4}{x+2}$ is strictly increasing on $[0,+\infty)$.
2.a. Prove by induction that for every natural number $n$,
$$0\leqslant u_n\leqslant u_{n+1}\leqslant 4.$$
2.b. Justify that the sequence $(u_n)$ is convergent.
3. We accept that for every natural number $n$,
$$0\leqslant 4-u_n\leqslant 3\times\left(\frac{1}{2}\right)^n.$$
Deduce the limit of the sequence $(u_n)$ and interpret it in the context of the model.

Geometry in space.

In an orthonormal coordinate system of space, consider the points
$$A(2,-1,0),\quad B(3,-1,2),\quad C(0,4,1)\quad\text{and}\quad S(0,1,4).$$
1. Show that the triangle ABC is right-angled at A.
2.a. Show that the vector $\overrightarrow{n}\begin{pmatrix}2\\1\\-1\end{pmatrix}$ is orthogonal to the plane (ABC).
2.b. Deduce a Cartesian equation of the plane (ABC).
2.c. Show that the points A, B, C and S are not coplanar.
3. Let $(d)$ be the line orthogonal to the plane (ABC) passing through S. It meets the plane (ABC) at H.
3.a. Determine a parametric representation of the line $(d)$.
3.b. Show that the coordinates of the point H are $H(2,2,3)$.
4. Recall that the volume $V$ of a tetrahedron is $V=\dfrac{\text{area of the base}\times\text{height}}{3}$.
Calculate the volume of the tetrahedron SABC.
5.a. Calculate the length SA.
5.b. We are told that $SB=\sqrt{17}$.
Deduce a measure of the angle $\widehat{ASB}$ to the nearest tenth of a degree.

Differential equations.

Part A
Let $g$ be the function defined on $\mathbb{R}$ by
$$g(x)=2e^{-\frac{1}{3}x}+\frac{2}{3}x-2.$$
1. We accept that the function $g$ is differentiable on $\mathbb{R}$ and denote by $g'$ its derivative.
Show that, for every real number $x$,
$$g'(x)=\frac{-2}{3}e^{-\frac{1}{3}x}+\frac{2}{3}.$$
2. Deduce the monotonicity of the function $g$ on $\mathbb{R}$.
3. Determine the sign of $g(x)$ for every real $x$.

Part B
1. Consider the differential equation
$$(E):\quad 3y'+y=0.$$
Solve the differential equation $(E)$.
2. Determine the particular solution whose graph, in a coordinate system of the plane, passes through the point $M(0,2)$.
3. Let $f$ be the function defined on $\mathbb{R}$ by
$$f(x)=2e^{-\frac{1}{3}x}$$
and $\mathcal{C}_f$ its graph.
3.a. Show that the tangent $(\Delta_0)$ to the curve $\mathcal{C}_f$ at the point $M(0,2)$ has an equation of the form
$$y=-\frac{2}{3}x+2.$$
3.b. Study, on $\mathbb{R}$, the position of the curve $\mathcal{C}_f$ relative to the tangent $(\Delta_0)$.

Part C
1. Let A be the point of the curve $\mathcal{C}_f$ with abscissa $a$, where $a$ is any real number.
Show that the tangent $(\Delta_a)$ to the curve $\mathcal{C}_f$ at the point A meets the $x$-axis at a point P with abscissa $a+3$.
2. Explain the construction of the tangent $(\Delta_{-2})$ to the curve $\mathcal{C}_f$ at the point B with abscissa $-2$.

This exercise is a multiple-choice questionnaire. For each of the five questions, four answers are proposed; exactly one of these answers is correct. No justification of the choice is required.

Question 1:
Consider the function $g$ defined on $(0,+\infty)$ by $g(x)=x^2+2x-\dfrac{3}{x}$.

On 1 January 2020, the Big Sun solar power plant had 10560 solar panels.
It is observed every year that $2\,\%$ of the panels have deteriorated and must be removed, while 250 new solar panels are installed.

Part A – Modelling with a sequence
The evolution of the number of solar panels is modelled by the sequence $(u_n)$ defined by $u_0=10560$ and, for every natural number $n$, $u_{n+1}=0.98u_n+250$, where $u_n$ is the number of solar panels on 1 January of the year $2020+n$.
1.a. Explain how this model corresponds to the situation studied.
1.b. We want to know after how many years the number of solar panels will be strictly greater than 12000.
Using a calculator, give the answer to this problem.
1.c. Copy and complete the following Python program so that the value sought in the previous question is stored in the variable n at the end of its execution.
$$\begin{array}{l}\text{u = 10560}\\ \text{n = 0}\\ \text{while ......:}\\ \quad\text{u = ......}\\ \quad\text{n = ......}\end{array}$$
2. Prove by induction that, for every natural number $n$, $u_n\leqslant 12500$.
3. Prove that the sequence $(u_n)$ is increasing.
4. Deduce that the sequence $(u_n)$ converges. You are not asked to compute its limit here.
5. Define the sequence $(v_n)$ by $v_n=u_n-12500$ for every natural number $n$.
5.a. Prove that the sequence $(v_n)$ is a geometric sequence with common ratio $0.98$, and give its first term.
5.b. Express $v_n$ in terms of $n$ for every natural number $n$.
5.c. Deduce $u_n$ in terms of $n$ for every natural number $n$.
5.d. Determine the limit of the sequence $(u_n)$.
Interpret this result in the context of the model.

Part B – Modelling with a function
A more precise model made it possible to estimate the number of solar panels of the plant by the function $f$ defined for every $x\in[0,+\infty)$ by
$$f(x)=12500-500e^{-0.02x+1.4},$$
where $x$ is the number of years elapsed since 1 January 2020.
1. Study the monotonicity of the function $f$.
2. Determine the limit of the function $f$ at $+\infty$.
3. Using this model, determine after how many years the number of solar panels will exceed 12000.

Part A
In a country, a disease affects the population with probability $0.05$.
A screening test for this disease is available.
Consider a sample of $n$ people ($n\geqslant 20$) taken at random from the population, treated as drawing with replacement.
The sample is tested by the following method: the blood of these $n$ individuals is mixed and the mixture is tested.
If the test is positive, an individual analysis of each person is carried out.
Let $X_n$ be the random variable giving the number of analyses carried out.
1. Show that $X_n$ takes the values $1$ and $(n+1)$.
2. Prove that $P(X_n=1)=0.95^n$.
Establish the distribution of $X_n$ by copying onto your answer sheet and completing the following table:
$$\begin{array}{|c|c|c|}\hline x_i&1&n+1\\ \hline P(X_n=x_i)&&\\ \hline\end{array}$$
3. What does the expectation of $X_n$ represent in the context of the experiment?
Show that $E(X_n)=n+1-n\times 0.95^n$.

Part B
1. Consider the function $f$ defined on $[20,+\infty)$ by $f(x)=\ln(x)+x\ln(0.95)$.
Show that $f$ is decreasing on $[20,+\infty)$.
2. Recall that $\displaystyle\lim_{x\to+\infty}\frac{\ln x}{x}=0$. Show that $\displaystyle\lim_{x\to+\infty}f(x)=-\infty$.
3. Show that $f(x)=0$ has a unique solution $a$ on $[20,+\infty)$.
Give a bound of this solution to within $0.1$.
4. Deduce the sign of $f$ on $[20,+\infty)$.

Part C
We want to compare two types of screening.
The first method is described in Part A; the second, more classical, consists in testing all individuals.
The first method reduces the number of analyses as soon as $E(X_n)<n$.
Using Part B, show that the first method reduces the number of analyses for samples of at most 87 people.

In the Pyrenees National Park, a researcher is working on the decline of a protected species in high-mountain lakes: the "midwife toad".
Parts I and II can be treated independently.

Part I: Effect of introducing a new species
In some lakes of the Pyrenees, trout have been introduced by humans to allow fishing activities in the mountains. The researcher studied the impact of this introduction on the population of midwife toads in a lake.
His previous studies lead him to model the evolution of this population as a function of time by the following function $f$:
$$f(t)=\left(0.04t^2-8t+400\right)e^{\frac{t}{50}}+40\quad\text{for } t\in[0,120].$$
The variable $t$ represents the time elapsed, in days, from the introduction of the trout into the lake at the instant $t=0$, and $f(t)$ models the number of toads at the instant $t$.
1. Determine the number of toads present in the lake when the trout were introduced.
2. We accept that the function $f$ is differentiable on the interval $[0,120]$ and denote by $f'$ its derivative.
Show, displaying the steps of the calculation, that for every real number $t$ in the interval $[0,120]$,
$$f'(t)=t(t-100)e^{\frac{t}{50}}\times 8\times 10^{-4}.$$
3. Study the variations of the function $f$ on the interval $[0,120]$, then draw up the table of variations of $f$ on this interval (give approximate values to the nearest hundredth).
4. According to this model:
4.a. Determine the number of days $J$ needed for the number of toads to reach its minimum. What is this minimum number?
4.b. Justify that, after reaching its minimum, the number of toads will one day exceed 140 individuals.
4.c. Using a calculator, determine the duration in days from which the number of toads will exceed 140 individuals.

Part II: Effect of chytridiomycosis on a population of tadpoles
One of the main causes of the decline of this species of toad in high mountains is a disease, "chytridiomycosis", caused by a fungus.
The researcher considers that:
• three quarters of the mountain lakes of the Pyrenees are not infected by the fungus, that is, they contain no contaminated tadpole (larva of the toad);
• in the remaining lakes, the probability that a tadpole is contaminated is $0.74$.
The researcher chooses a lake of the Pyrenees at random and takes samples there.
For the rest of the exercise, results are to be rounded to the nearest thousandth when necessary.
The researcher takes a tadpole at random from the chosen lake in order to test it before releasing it.
Let $T$ be the event "the tadpole is contaminated by the disease" and $L$ the event "the lake is infected by the fungus".
Let $\overline{L}$ be the complementary event of $L$ and $\overline{T}$ the complementary event of $T$.
1. Copy and complete the following probability tree using the data of the statement: first level $L$, $\overline{L}$; second level $T$, $\overline{T}$; on the branches from $\overline{L}$ the probabilities $0$ (to $T$) and $1$ (to $\overline{T}$) are already given.
2. Show that the probability $P(T)$ that the tadpole taken is contaminated is $0.185$.
3. The tadpole is not contaminated. What is the probability that the lake is infected?

Main topics: logarithm function.

Part I
Consider the function $h$ defined on the interval $(0,+\infty)$ by
$$h(x)=1+\frac{\ln(x)}{x}.$$
1. Determine the limit of the function $h$ at $0$.
2. Determine the limit of the function $h$ at $+\infty$.
3. Let $h'$ denote the derivative of $h$. Prove that, for every real number $x$ in $(0,+\infty)$,
$$h'(x)=\frac{1-\ln(x)}{x^2}.$$
4. Draw up the table of variations of the function $h$ on the interval $(0,+\infty)$.
5. Prove that the equation $h(x)=0$ has a unique solution $\alpha$ in $(0,+\infty)$.
Justify that $0.5<\alpha<0.6$.

Part II
In this part, consider the functions $f$ and $g$ defined on $(0,+\infty)$ by
$$f(x)=x\ln(x)-x;\qquad g(x)=\ln(x).$$
Let $\mathcal{C}_f$ and $\mathcal{C}_g$ be the curves representing the functions $f$ and $g$ respectively in an orthonormal coordinate system $\left(O;\overrightarrow{i},\overrightarrow{j}\right)$.
For every strictly positive real number $a$, we call:
• $T_a$ the tangent to $\mathcal{C}_f$ at its point with abscissa $a$;
• $D_a$ the tangent to $\mathcal{C}_g$ at its point with abscissa $a$.
The curves $\mathcal{C}_f$ and $\mathcal{C}_g$ as well as two tangents $T_a$ and $D_a$ are shown in the figure.
We look for possible values of $a$ for which the lines $T_a$ and $D_a$ are perpendicular.
Let $a$ be a real number in the interval $(0,+\infty)$.
1. Justify that the line $D_a$ has slope $\dfrac{1}{a}$.
2. Justify that the line $T_a$ has slope $\ln(a)$.
Recall that in an orthonormal coordinate system, two lines with slopes $m$ and $m'$ respectively are perpendicular if and only if $mm'=-1$.
3. Prove that there exists a unique value of $a$, which you will identify, for which the lines $T_a$ and $D_a$ are perpendicular.

A company receives numerous e-mails every day.
Among these e-mails, $8\,\%$ are "spam", that is, messages with advertising or even malicious intent, which it is preferable not to open.
An e-mail received by the company is chosen at random.
The properties of the e-mail software used in the company make it possible to state that:
• the probability that the chosen e-mail is classified as "unwanted" given that it is spam is equal to $0.9$;
• the probability that the chosen e-mail is classified as "unwanted" given that it is not spam is equal to $0.01$.
We denote:
• $S$ the event "the chosen e-mail is spam";
• $I$ the event "the chosen e-mail is classified as unwanted by the e-mail software";
• $\overline{S}$ and $\overline{I}$ the complementary events of $S$ and $I$ respectively.
1. Model the situation studied by a weighted tree, showing the probabilities associated with each branch.
2.a. Prove that the probability that the chosen e-mail is a spam message and is classified as unwanted is equal to $0.072$.
2.b. Calculate the probability that the chosen message is classified as unwanted.
2.c. The chosen message is classified as unwanted. What is the probability that it is actually a spam message? Give the result rounded to the nearest hundredth.
3. 50 e-mails are chosen at random among those received by the company. We accept that this choice amounts to drawing 50 e-mails at random with replacement from all the e-mails received by the company.
Let $Z$ be the random variable counting the spam e-mails among the 50 chosen.
3.a. What is the probability distribution of the random variable $Z$, and what are its parameters?
3.b. What is the probability that, among the 50 chosen e-mails, at least two are spam? Give the result rounded to the nearest hundredth.

In a clinical trial, two treatment protocols for a disease are being considered.
The aim of this exercise is to study, for these two protocols, the evolution of the quantity of drug present in a patient's blood as a function of time.
Parts A and B are independent.

Part A: Study of the first protocol
The first protocol consists in having the patient take a drug in tablet form.
The quantity of drug present in the patient's blood, expressed in mg, is modelled by the function $f$ defined on the interval $[0,10]$ by
$$f(t)=3te^{-0.5t+1},$$
where $t$ denotes the time, in hours, elapsed since the tablet was taken.
1.a. We accept that the function $f$ is differentiable on the interval $[0,10]$ and denote by $f'$ its derivative.
Show that, for every real number $t$ in $[0,10]$, $f'(t)=3(-0.5t+1)e^{-0.5t+1}$.
1.b. Deduce the table of variations of the function $f$ on the interval $[0,10]$.
1.c. According to this model, after how much time will the quantity of drug present in the patient's blood be maximal?
What is this maximal quantity?
2.a. Show that the equation $f(t)=5$ has a unique solution on the interval $[0,2]$, denoted $\alpha$, and give an approximate value of it to within $10^{-2}$.
We accept that the equation $f(t)=5$ has a unique solution on the interval $[2,10]$, denoted $\beta$, and that an approximate value of $\beta$ to within $10^{-2}$ is $3.46$.
2.b. The treatment is considered effective when the quantity of drug present in the patient's blood is greater than or equal to $5$ mg.
Determine, to the nearest minute, the duration of effectiveness of the drug in the case of this protocol.

Part B: Study of the second protocol
The second protocol consists in initially injecting the patient intravenously with a dose of $2$ mg of the drug, then re-injecting a dose of $1.8$ mg every hour.
We assume that the drug spreads instantly in the blood and is then gradually eliminated.
It is estimated that one hour after an injection, the quantity of drug in the blood has decreased by $30\,\%$ compared with the quantity present immediately after this injection.
This situation is modelled by the sequence $(u_n)$ where, for every natural number $n$, $u_n$ denotes the quantity of drug, in mg, present in the patient's blood immediately after the injection of the $n$-th hour. Thus $u_0=2$.
1. Calculate, according to this model, the quantity $u_1$ of drug (in mg) present in the patient's blood immediately after the injection of the first hour.
2. Justify that, for every natural number $n$, $u_{n+1}=0.7u_n+1.8$.
3.a. Show by induction that, for every natural number $n$, $u_n\leqslant u_{n+1}<6$.
3.b. Deduce that the sequence $(u_n)$ is convergent. Let $\ell$ be its limit.
3.c. Determine the value of $\ell$. Interpret this value in the context of the exercise.
4. Consider the sequence $(v_n)$ defined, for every natural number $n$, by $v_n=6-u_n$.
4.a. Show that the sequence $(v_n)$ is a geometric sequence with common ratio $0.7$, and give its first term.
4.b. Determine the expression of $v_n$ in terms of $n$, then of $u_n$ in terms of $n$.

Topics: logarithm function and sequence.

Let $f$ be the function defined on the interval $(0,+\infty)$ by
$$f(x)=x\ln(x)+1.$$
Let $\mathcal{C}_f$ be its graph in a coordinate system of the plane.
1. Determine the limit of the function $f$ at 0 as well as its limit at $+\infty$.
2.a. We accept that $f$ is differentiable on $(0,+\infty)$ and denote by $f'$ its derivative.
Show that for every strictly positive real $x$,
$$f'(x)=1+\ln(x).$$
2.b. Deduce the table of variations of the function $f$ on $(0,+\infty)$. Include the exact value of the extremum of $f$ on $(0,+\infty)$ and the limits.
2.c. Justify that for every $x\in(0,1)$, $f(x)\in(0,1)$.

$$f(x)\geqslant x.$$

$$u_{n+1}=f(u_n).$$
4.a. Prove by induction that for every natural number $n$, $0<u_n<1$.
4.b. Deduce from question 3.c. that the sequence $(u_n)$ is increasing.

Topic: probability.

An urn contains white and black tokens, all indistinguishable to the touch.
A game consists in drawing at random, successively and with replacement, two tokens from this urn.
The following rule of the game is established:
• a player loses 9 euros if the two tokens drawn are both white;
• a player loses 1 euro if the two tokens drawn are both black;
• a player wins 5 euros if the two tokens drawn are of different colours.
1. Assume that the urn contains 2 black tokens and 3 white tokens.
1.a. Model the situation with a weighted tree.
1.b. Calculate the probability of losing 9 euros in one game.
2. Assume now that the urn contains 3 white tokens and at least two black tokens, but the exact number of black tokens is unknown. Let $N$ be the number of black tokens.
2.a. Let $X$ be the random variable giving the gain of the game for one game.
Determine the probability distribution of this random variable.
2.b. Solve, for real $x$, the inequality
$$-x^2+30x-81>0.$$
2.c. Using the result of the previous question, determine the number of black tokens that the urn must contain for this game to be favourable to the player.
2.d. How many black tokens should the player ask for in order to obtain a maximal mean gain?
3. We observe 10 players who try their luck by playing one game each, independently of one another. Assume that 7 black tokens have been placed in the urn (with 3 white tokens).
What is the probability of having at least 1 player winning 5 euros?

Topic: probability.

A hotel located near a tourist site devoted to prehistory offers two visits in the surroundings, one of a museum and one of a cave.
A study has shown that $70\,\%$ of the hotel's guests visit the museum. Moreover, among the guests visiting the museum, $60\,\%$ visit the cave.
This study also shows that $6\,\%$ of the hotel's guests make no visit.
A guest of the hotel is interviewed at random and we denote:
• $M$ the event: "the guest visits the museum";
• $G$ the event: "the guest visits the cave".
Let $\overline{M}$ be the complementary event of $M$, $\overline{G}$ the complementary event of $G$, and for every event $E$, let $p(E)$ be the probability of $E$.
Thus, according to the statement, $p\left(\overline{M}\cap\overline{G}\right)=0.06$.
1.a. Check that $p_{\overline{M}}\left(\overline{G}\right)=0.2$, where $p_{\overline{M}}\left(\overline{G}\right)$ denotes the probability that the guest interviewed does not visit the cave given that he does not visit the museum.
1.b. A weighted tree (first level $M$, $\overline{M}$; second level $G$, $\overline{G}$) models the situation. Copy and complete this tree by indicating on each branch the associated probability.
1.c. What is the probability of the event "the guest visits the cave and does not visit the museum"?
1.d. Show that $p(G)=0.66$.
2. The hotel manager states that among the guests who visit the cave, more than half also visit the museum. Is this statement correct?
3. The prices of the visits are as follows:
• visit of the museum: 12 euros;
• visit of the cave: 5 euros.
Consider the random variable $T$ modelling the sum spent by a guest of the hotel on these visits.
3.a. Give the probability distribution of $T$. Present the results in a table.
3.b. Calculate the mathematical expectation of $T$.
3.c. For reasons of profitability, the hotel manager considers that the mean amount of the takings from the visits must be greater than 700 euros per day.
Determine the mean number of guests per day that makes it possible to reach this objective.
4. To increase the takings, the manager wants the expectation of the random variable modelling the sum spent by a guest of the hotel on these visits to become 15 euros, without changing the price of the museum visit, which remains 12 euros.
What price should be set for the visit of the cave to reach this objective? (We accept that the increase in the price of the cave does not change the attendance of the two sites.)
5. 100 guests of the hotel are chosen at random, this choice being treated as drawing with replacement.
What is the probability that at least three quarters of these guests visited the cave during their stay at the hotel?
Give the result to within $10^{-3}$.

Topics: logarithm and exponential functions, sequences.

Part A
Consider the function $f$ defined on the interval $[1,+\infty)$ by
$$f(x)=\frac{\ln x}{x},$$
where ln denotes the natural logarithm function.
1. Give the limit of the function $f$ at $+\infty$.
2. We accept that the function $f$ is differentiable on the interval $[1,+\infty)$ and denote by $f'$ its derivative.
2.a. Show that, for every real number $x\geqslant 1$, $f'(x)=\dfrac{1-\ln x}{x^2}$.
2.b. Justify the following sign table, giving the sign of $f'(x)$ according to the values of $x$.
$$\begin{array}{c|ccccc}x&1&&e&&+\infty\\ \hline f'(x)&&+&0&-&\end{array}$$
2.c. Draw up the complete table of variations of the function $f$.

3.a. Show that, if $0\leqslant k\leqslant\dfrac{1}{e}$, the equation $f(x)=k$ has a unique solution on the interval $[1,e]$.
3.b. If $k>\dfrac{1}{e}$, does the equation $f(x)=k$ have solutions on the interval $[1,+\infty)$? Justify.

Part B
Let $g$ be the function defined on $\mathbb{R}$ by
$$g(x)=e^{\frac{x}{4}}.$$
Consider the sequence $(u_n)$ defined by $u_0=1$ and, for every natural number $n$,
$u_{n+1}=e^{\frac{u_n}{4}}$, that is, $u_{n+1}=g(u_n)$.
1. Justify that the function $g$ is increasing on $\mathbb{R}$.
2. Show by induction that, for every natural number $n$, $u_n\leqslant u_{n+1}\leqslant e$.

Let $\ell$ be the limit of the sequence $(u_n)$; we accept that $\ell$ is a solution of the equation
$$e^{\frac{x}{4}}=x.$$

5. Give an approximate value to within $10^{-2}$ of the limit $\ell$ of the sequence $(u_n)$.

Topic: probability.

In Hugo's shop, customers can rent two types of bicycles: road bikes or mountain bikes.
Each type of bicycle can be rented in its electric version or not.
A customer of the shop is chosen at random, and we accept that:
— if the customer rents a road bike, the probability that it is an electric bike is $0.4$;
— if the customer rents a mountain bike, the probability that it is an electric bike is $0.7$;
— the probability that the customer rents an electric bike is $0.58$.
Let $\alpha$ be the probability that the customer rents a road bike, with $0\leqslant\alpha\leqslant 1$.
Consider the following events:
• $R$: "the customer rents a road bike";
• $E$: "the customer rents an electric bike";
• $\overline{R}$ and $\overline{E}$, the complementary events of $R$ and $E$.
This random situation is modelled by a tree: first level $R$ with probability $\alpha$ and $\overline{R}$ with probability $1-\alpha$; second level $E$, $\overline{E}$ (probabilities to be filled in).
If $F$ denotes any event, $p(F)$ denotes the probability of $F$.
1. Copy this tree onto your answer sheet and complete it.
2.a. Show that $p(E)=0.7-0.3\alpha$.
2.b. Deduce that $\alpha=0.4$.
3. We know that the customer rented an electric bike.
Determine the probability that he rented a mountain bike. Give the result rounded to the nearest hundredth.
4. What is the probability that the customer rents an electric mountain bike?
5. The price of renting a non-electric road bike for a day is 25 euros, that of a non-electric mountain bike 35 euros.
For each type of bicycle, choosing the electric version increases the daily rental price by 15 euros.
Let $X$ be the random variable modelling the daily rental price of a bicycle.
5.a. Give the probability distribution of $X$. Present the results in a table.
5.b. Calculate the mathematical expectation of $X$ and interpret this result.
6. When 30 of Hugo's customers are chosen at random, this choice is treated as drawing with replacement.
Let $Y$ be the random variable associating with a sample of 30 customers chosen at random the number of customers who rent an electric bike.
Recall that the probability of the event $E$ is $p(E)=0.58$.
6.a. Justify that $Y$ follows a binomial distribution, and give its parameters.
6.b. Determine the probability that a sample contains exactly 20 customers who rent an electric bike. Give the result rounded to the nearest thousandth.
6.c. Determine the probability that a sample contains at least 15 customers who rent an electric bike. Give the result rounded to the nearest thousandth.

Topics: logarithm function, sequences.

Parts B and C are independent.
Consider the function $f$ defined on $(0,+\infty)$ by
$$f(x)=x-x\ln x,$$
where ln denotes the natural logarithm function.

Part A
1. Determine the limit of $f(x)$ as $x$ tends to 0.
2. Determine the limit of $f(x)$ as $x$ tends to $+\infty$.
3. We accept that the function $f$ is differentiable on $(0,+\infty)$ and denote by $f'$ its derivative.
3.a. Prove that, for every real $x>0$, $f'(x)=-\ln x$.
3.b. Deduce the variations of the function $f$ on $(0,+\infty)$ and draw up its table of variations.
4. Solve the equation $f(x)=x$ on $(0,+\infty)$.

Part B
In this part, some results of Part A may usefully be used.
Consider the sequence $(u_n)$ defined by
$$\left\{\begin{array}{rcl}u_0&=&0.5\\ u_{n+1}&=&u_n-u_n\ln u_n\ \text{ for every natural number } n.\end{array}\right.$$
Thus, for every natural number $n$, $u_{n+1}=f(u_n)$.
1. Recall that the function $f$ is increasing on the interval $[0.5,1]$.
Prove by induction that, for every natural number $n$, $0.5\leqslant u_n\leqslant u_{n+1}\leqslant 1$.

Part C
For any real number $k$, consider the function $f_k$ defined on $(0,+\infty)$ by
$$f_k(x)=kx-x\ln x.$$

This exercise is a multiple-choice questionnaire. For each question, exactly one of the four proposed answers is correct. No justification is required. The questions are independent.

A technician inspects the machines equipping a large company. All these machines are identical.

Consider the function $f$ defined on $(0,+\infty)$ by

A company has created a Frequently Asked Questions page ("FAQ") on its website.
We study the number of questions posted there each month.

Part A: First model
In this part, we accept that, each month:
• $90\,\%$ of the questions already posted the previous month are kept on the FAQ;
• 130 new questions are added to the FAQ.
During the first month, 300 questions were posted.
To estimate the number of questions, in hundreds, present on the FAQ in the $n$-th month, the situation above is modelled by the sequence $(u_n)$ defined by

$$u_n=13-\frac{100}{9}\times 0.9^n.$$

Biologists are studying the evolution of a population of insects in a botanical garden.
At the beginning of the study the population is 100000 insects.
To preserve the balance of the natural environment, the number of insects must not exceed 400000.

Part A: Study of a first model in the laboratory
Observation of the evolution of these populations of insects in the laboratory, in the absence of any predator, shows that the number of insects increases by $60\,\%$ each month.
Taking this observation into account, the biologists model the evolution of the insect population by a sequence $(u_n)$ where, for every natural number $n$, $u_n$ models the number of insects, in millions, after $n$ months.

3. By solving an inequality, determine the smallest natural number $n$ from which $u_n>0.4$.

Parts A and B are independent.

To help detect certain allergies, a blood test can be carried out, whose result is either positive or negative.
In a population, this test gives the following results:
• if an individual is allergic, the test is positive in $97\,\%$ of cases;
• if an individual is not allergic, the test is negative in $95.7\,\%$ of cases.
Moreover, $20\,\%$ of the individuals of the population concerned have a positive test.
An individual is chosen at random from the population, and we denote:
• $A$ the event "the individual is allergic";
• $T$ the event "the individual has a positive test".
Let $\overline{A}$ and $\overline{T}$ denote the complementary events of $A$ and $T$. Let $x$ be the probability of the event $A$: $x=p(A)$.

Part A

2.b. Deduce the probability that the chosen individual is allergic.

"If the test of an individual chosen at random is positive, there is more than an $80\,\%$ chance that this individual is allergic."

Part A: study of the function $f$
The function $f$ is defined on the interval $]0;+\infty[$ by
$$f(x)=x-2+\frac{1}{2}\ln x,$$
where $\ln$ denotes the natural logarithm function. It is given that the function $f$ is twice differentiable on $]0;+\infty[$; $f'$ denotes its derivative and $f''$ its second derivative.
1.a. Determine, with justification, the limits of $f$ at $0$ and at $+\infty$.
1.b. Show that for every $x$ in $]0;+\infty[$, $f'(x)=\frac{2x+1}{2x}$.
1.c. Study the direction of variation of $f$ on $]0;+\infty[$.
1.d. Study the convexity of $f$ on $]0;+\infty[$.
2.a. Show that the equation $f(x)=0$ has a unique solution in $]0;+\infty[$, denoted $\alpha$, and justify that $\alpha$ belongs to the interval $[1;2]$.
2.b. Determine the sign of $f(x)$ for $x\in\,]0;+\infty[$.
2.c. Show that $\ln(\alpha)=2(2-\alpha)$.

Part B: study of the function $g$
The function $g$ is defined on $]0;1]$ by
$$g(x)=-\frac{7}{8}x^2+x-\frac{1}{4}x^2\ln x.$$
It is given that the function $g$ is differentiable on $]0;1]$; $g'$ denotes its derivative.
1. Compute $g'(x)$ for $x\in\,]0;1]$, then check that $g'(x)=xf\left(\frac{1}{x}\right)$.

$$\begin{array}{c|ccccc}x & 0 & & \frac{1}{\alpha} & & 1\\ \hline \text{sign of } f\left(\frac{1}{x}\right) & \| & + & 0 & - & \end{array}$$

1.a. Justify the relative position of the curves $\mathcal{C}_g$ and $\mathcal{P}$ on the interval $]0;1]$.
1.b. Prove the equality
$$\int_{\frac{1}{\alpha}}^{1}x^2\ln x\,\mathrm{d}x=\frac{-\alpha^3-6\alpha+13}{9\alpha^3}.$$

The head of a school wishes to carry out a study of the students who took the final examination, to analyse how well they think they did in this examination.
For this study, at the end of the examination the students are asked to answer individually the question: "Do you think you passed the examination?".
Only the answers "yes" or "no" are possible, and it is observed that $91.7\,\%$ of the students questioned answered "yes".
After the publication of the examination results, it is found that:
• $65\,\%$ of the students who failed answered "no";
• $98\,\%$ of the students who passed answered "yes".
A student who took the examination is questioned at random.
Let $R$ be the event "the student passed the examination" and $Q$ the event "the student answered "yes" to the question".
For any event $A$, $P(A)$ denotes its probability and $\overline{A}$ its complementary event.
Throughout the exercise, probabilities are rounded to $10^{-3}$ if necessary.
1. Give the values of the probabilities $P(Q)$ and $P_{\overline{R}}\left(\overline{Q}\right)$.
2. Let $x$ be the probability that the student questioned passed the examination.
2.a. Copy and complete the weighted tree below: first branches to $R$ (probability $x$) and to $\overline{R}$ (probability $\ldots$); from each of $R$ and $\overline{R}$, branches to $Q$ and $\overline{Q}$ with probabilities $\ldots$.
2.b. Show that $x=0.9$.
3. The student questioned answered "yes" to the question.
What is the probability that he passed the examination?
4. The mark obtained by a student questioned at random is a whole number between $0$ and $20$. It is assumed that it is modelled by a random variable $N$ following the binomial distribution with parameters $(20;0.615)$.
The head wishes to give a reward to the students who obtained the best results.
From which mark onward must she give the rewards so that $65\,\%$ of the students are rewarded?
5. Ten students are questioned at random.
The random variables $N_1,N_2,\ldots,N_{10}$ model the mark out of $20$ obtained in the examination by each of them. It is given that these variables are independent and follow the same binomial distribution with parameters $(20;0.615)$.
Let $S$ be the variable defined by $S=N_1+N_2+\cdots+N_{10}$.
Compute the expected value $E(S)$ and the variance $V(S)$ of the random variable $S$.
6. Consider the random variable $M=\frac{S}{10}$.
6.a. What does this random variable $M$ model in the context of the exercise?
6.b. Justify that $E(M)=12.3$ and $V(M)=0.47355$.
6.c. Using the Bienaymé–Chebyshev inequality, justify the statement below:
"The probability that the mean of the marks of ten students taken at random lies strictly between $10.3$ and $14.3$ is at least $80\,\%$."

Alain owns a swimming pool containing $50\ \text{m}^3$ of water. Recall that $1\ \text{m}^3=1000$ L.
To disinfect the water, he must add chlorine.
The chlorine level in the water, expressed in $\text{mg}\cdot\text{L}^{-1}$, is defined as the mass of chlorine per unit volume of water. Pool specialists recommend a chlorine level between $1$ and $3\ \text{mg}\cdot\text{L}^{-1}$.
Under the action of the environment, in particular ultraviolet light, chlorine decomposes and gradually disappears.
On certain days, at a fixed time, Alain takes measurements with a device accurate to $0.01\ \text{mg}\cdot\text{L}^{-1}$. On Wednesday 19 June, he measures a chlorine level of $0.70\ \text{mg}\cdot\text{L}^{-1}$.

Part A: study of a discrete model
To maintain the chlorine level in his pool, Alain decides, from Thursday 20 June onward, to add $15$ g of chlorine every day. It is assumed that this chlorine mixes uniformly in the water of the pool.
1. Justify that this addition of chlorine increases the level by $0.3\ \text{mg}\cdot\text{L}^{-1}$.
2. For every natural number $n$, let $v_n$ be the chlorine level, in $\text{mg}\cdot\text{L}^{-1}$, obtained with this new protocol $n$ days after Wednesday 19 June. Thus $v_0=0.7$.
It is given that for every natural number $n$,
$$v_{n+1}=0.92v_n+0.3.$$
2.a. Show by induction that for every natural number $n$, $v_n\leqslant v_{n+1}\leqslant 4$.
2.b. Show that the sequence $(v_n)$ is convergent and compute its limit.
3. In the long term, will the chlorine level comply with the pool specialists' recommendation? Justify the answer.
4. Reproduce and complete the algorithm below, written in Python, so that the function alerte_chlore returns, when it exists, the smallest integer $n$ such that $v_n>s$.
$$\begin{array}{l}\texttt{def alerte}\_\texttt{chlore(s) :}\\ \quad\texttt{n=0}\\ \quad\texttt{u = 0.7}\\ \quad\texttt{while ... :}\\ \quad\quad\texttt{n = ...}\\ \quad\quad\texttt{u = ...}\\ \quad\texttt{return n}\end{array}$$
5. What value is obtained by entering the instruction alerte_chlore(3)? Interpret this result in the context of the exercise.

Part B: study of a continuous model
Alain decides to call on a specialised consultancy. It uses a continuous model to describe the chlorine level in the pool.
In this model, for a duration $x$ (in days elapsed from Wednesday 19 June), $f(x)$ represents the chlorine level, in $\text{mg}\cdot\text{L}^{-1}$, in the pool.
It is given that the function $f$ is a solution of the differential equation $(E):\ y'=-0.08y+\frac{q}{50}$, where $q$ is the quantity of chlorine, in grams, added to the pool each day.
1. Justify that the function $f$ is of the form $f(x)=C\mathrm{e}^{-0.08x}+\frac{q}{4}$, where $C$ is a real constant.
2.a. Express in terms of $q$ the limit of $f$ at $+\infty$.
2.b. Recall that the chlorine level observed on Wednesday 19 June is equal to $0.7\ \text{mg}\cdot\text{L}^{-1}$.
We want the chlorine level to stabilise in the long term around $2\ \text{mg}\cdot\text{L}^{-1}$.
Determine the values of $C$ and $q$ so that these two conditions are satisfied.

A robot is placed on a horizontal axis and moves several times by one metre along this axis, randomly to the right or to the left.
On the first move, the probability that the robot moves to the right is equal to $\frac{1}{3}$.
If it moves to the right, the probability that the robot moves to the right again on the next move is equal to $\frac{3}{4}$.
If it moves to the left, the probability that the robot moves to the left again on the next move is equal to $\frac{1}{2}$.
For every natural number $n\geqslant 1$, let:
• $D_n$ be the event "the robot moves to the right on the $n$-th move";
• $\overline{D_n}$ be the complementary event of $D_n$;
• $p_n$ be the probability of the event $D_n$.
Thus $p_1=\frac{1}{3}$.

In this part, the robot makes two successive moves.

• $15\,\%$ of the connections pass through server $B$;
• the remaining connections go through server $C$.
Remote connections are sometimes unstable and, during normal operation of the servers, users may be disconnected for various reasons (server saturation, insufficient internet bandwidth, malicious attacks, software updates, etc.).
A connection is said to be stable if the user is not disconnected after logging in to the servers. The IT maintenance team has observed statistically that, under the usual operation of the servers:
• $90\,\%$ of the connections through server $A$ are stable;
• $80\,\%$ of the connections through server $B$ are stable;
• $85\,\%$ of the connections through server $C$ are stable.

2. Show that, for every $x$ in the interval $]-1;+\infty[$,
$$f'(x)=\frac{100-2x-2x^2}{25(x+1)}.$$
3. Study the variations of the function $f$ on the interval $]-1;+\infty[$, then deduce that the function $f$ is strictly increasing on the interval $[2;6.5]$.
4. Let $h$ be the function defined on the interval $[2;6.5]$ by $h(x)=f(x)-x$.
The table of variations of the function $h$ is given below:
$$\begin{array}{c|ccccc}x & 2 & & m\approx 2.364 & & 6.5\\ \hline h(x) & h(2) & \nearrow & M\approx 2.265 & \searrow & h(6.5)\end{array}$$
Show that the equation $h(x)=0$ has a unique solution $\alpha\in[2;6.5]$.
5. Consider the following script, written in Python:
$$\begin{array}{l}\texttt{from math import *}\\ \\ \texttt{def f(x) :}\\ \quad\texttt{return 4*log(1+x)-(x**2)/25}\\ \\ \texttt{def bornes(n) :}\\ \quad\texttt{p = 1/10**n}\\ \quad\texttt{x = 6}\\ \quad\texttt{while f(x)-x > 0 :}\\ \quad\quad\texttt{x = x + p}\\ \quad\texttt{return (x-p, x)}\end{array}$$
Recall that in Python:
• the command log(x) returns the value $\ln x$;
• the command c**d returns the value of $c^d$.
5.a. Give the values returned by the command bornes(2).
Give the values rounded to the hundredth.
5.b. Interpret these values in the context of the exercise.

Part B
In this part, the results obtained in Part A may be used.
Consider the sequence $(u_n)$ defined by $u_0=2$ and, for every natural number $n$, $u_{n+1}=f(u_n)$.
1. Show by induction that for every natural number $n$,
$$2\leqslant u_n\leqslant u_{n+1}<6.5.$$
2. Deduce that the sequence $(u_n)$ converges to a limit $\ell$.
3. Recall that the real number $\alpha$ defined in Part A is the solution of the equation $h(x)=0$ on the interval $[2;6.5]$.
Justify that $\ell=\alpha$.

Part A
Consider the differential equation
$$(E_1):\quad y'+0.48y=\frac{1}{250},$$
where $y$ is a function of the variable $t$ belonging to the interval $[0;+\infty[$.
1. Consider the constant function $h$ defined on the interval $[0;+\infty[$ by $h(t)=\frac{1}{120}$.
Show that the function $h$ is a solution of the differential equation $(E_1)$.
2. Give the general form of the solutions of the differential equation $y'+0.48y=0$.
3. Deduce the set of solutions of the differential equation $(E_1)$.

Part B
We now study the evolution of a population of bacteria in a culture medium.
At time $t=0$, an initial population of $30000$ bacteria is introduced into the medium.
Let $p(t)$ be the quantity of bacteria, expressed in thousands of individuals, present in the medium after a time $t$, expressed in hours.
Thus $p(0)=30$.
It is given that the function $p$ defined on the interval $[0;+\infty[$ is differentiable and strictly positive on this interval, and that it is a solution of the differential equation $(E_2)$:
$$p'=\frac{1}{250}p\times(120-p).$$
Let $y$ be the strictly positive function on the interval $[0;+\infty[$ such that, for every $t$ in the interval $[0;+\infty[$, $p(t)=\frac{1}{y(t)}$.
1. Show that if $p$ is a solution of the differential equation $(E_2)$, then $y$ is a solution of the differential equation $(E_1):\ y'+0.48y=\frac{1}{250}$.
2. It is given, conversely, that if $y$ is a strictly positive solution of the differential equation $(E_1)$, then $p=\frac{1}{y}$ is a solution of the differential equation $(E_2)$.
Show that, for every $t$ in the interval $[0;+\infty[$,
$$p(t)=\frac{120}{1+K\mathrm{e}^{-0.48t}}\quad\text{with } K \text{ a real constant.}$$
3. Using the initial condition, determine the value of $K$.
4. Determine $\displaystyle\lim_{t\to+\infty}p(t)$. Give an interpretation of it in the context of the exercise.
5. Determine the time needed for the population of bacteria to exceed $60000$ individuals.
Give the result as a rounded value expressed in hours and minutes.

We wish to compare the evolution of an animal population in two distinct environments $A$ and $B$.
On 1 January 2025, $6000$ individuals are introduced into each of the environments $A$ and $B$.

Part A
In this part, we study the evolution of the population in environment $A$.
It is assumed that in this environment the evolution of the population is modelled by a geometric sequence $(u_n)$ with first term $u_0=6$ and common ratio $0.93$.
For every natural number $n$, $u_n$ represents the population on 1 January of the year $2025+n$, expressed in thousands of individuals.
1. Give, according to this model, the population on 1 January 2026.
2. For every natural number $n$, express $u_n$ in terms of $n$.
3. Determine the limit of the sequence $(u_n)$.
Interpret this result in the context of the exercise.

Part B
In this part, we study the evolution of the population in environment $B$.
It is assumed that in this environment the evolution of the population is modelled by the sequence $(v_n)$ defined by
$$v_0=6\ \text{ and, for every natural number } n,\ v_{n+1}=-0.05v_n^2+1.1v_n.$$
For every natural number $n$, $v_n$ represents the population on 1 January of the year $2025+n$, expressed in thousands of individuals.
1. Give, according to this model, the population on 1 January 2026.
Let $f$ be the function defined on the interval $[0;+\infty[$ by
$$f(x)=-0.05x^2+1.1x.$$
2. Prove that the function $f$ is increasing on the interval $[0;11]$.
3. Prove by induction that for every natural number $n$,
$$2\leqslant v_{n+1}\leqslant v_n\leqslant 6.$$
4. Deduce that the sequence $(v_n)$ converges to a limit $\ell$.
5.a. Justify that the limit $\ell$ satisfies $f(\ell)=\ell$, then deduce the value of $\ell$.
5.b. Interpret this result in the context of the exercise.

Part C
The aim of this part is to compare the evolution of the population in the two environments.
1. By solving an inequality, determine the year from which the population of environment $A$ will be strictly less than $3000$ individuals.
2. Using a calculator, determine the year from which the population of environment $B$ will be strictly less than $3000$ individuals.
3. Justify that from a certain year onward, the population of environment $B$ will exceed the population of environment $A$.
4. Consider the Python program below.
$$\begin{array}{l}\texttt{n=0}\\ \texttt{u = 6}\\ \texttt{v = 6}\\ \texttt{while ... :}\\ \quad\texttt{u = ...}\\ \quad\texttt{v= ...}\\ \quad\texttt{n = n+1}\\ \texttt{print (2025 + n)}\end{array}$$
4.a. Copy and complete this program so that, after execution, it displays the year from which the population of environment $B$ is strictly greater than the population of environment $A$.
4.b. Determine the year displayed after execution of the program.

The "base64" encoding, used in computing, makes it possible to represent and transmit messages and other data such as images, using $64$ characters: the $26$ capital letters, the $26$ lower-case letters, the digits from $0$ to $9$ and two other special characters.
Parts A, B and C are independent.

Part A
In this part, we consider sequences of $4$ characters in base64. For example, "gP3g" is such a sequence. In a sequence, order matters: the sequences "m5C2" and "5C2m" are not identical.
1. Determine the number of possible sequences.
2. Determine the number of sequences if the $4$ characters are required to be pairwise distinct.
3.a. Determine the number of sequences containing no capital letter A.
3.b. Deduce the number of sequences containing at least one capital letter A.
3.c. Determine the number of sequences containing the capital letter A exactly once.
3.d. Determine the number of sequences containing the capital letter A exactly twice.

Part B
We consider the transmission of a sequence of $250$ characters from one computer to another. It is assumed that the probability that a character is wrongly transmitted is equal to $0.01$ and that the transmissions of the different characters are mutually independent. Let $X$ be the random variable equal to the number of wrongly transmitted characters.
1. It is given that the random variable $X$ follows a binomial distribution. Give its parameters.
2. Determine the probability that all the characters are correctly transmitted. Give the exact expression, then an approximate value to $10^{-3}$.
3. What do you think of the following statement: "The probability that more than $16$ characters are wrongly transmitted is negligible"?

Part C
We now consider the transmission of $4$ sequences of $250$ characters.

It is given that the random variables $X_1$, $X_2$, $X_3$ and $X_4$ are mutually independent and follow the same distribution as the random variable $X$ defined in Part B.
Let $S=X_1+X_2+X_3+X_4$.
Determine, with justification, the expected value and the variance of the random variable $S$.

There are four blood groups in the human species: A, B, AB and O.
Each blood group may carry a rhesus factor. When it is present, the rhesus is said to be positive; otherwise it is said to be negative.
Within the French population, it is known that:
• $45\,\%$ of individuals belong to group A, and among them $85\,\%$ are rhesus positive;
• $10\,\%$ of individuals belong to group B, and among them $84\,\%$ are rhesus positive;
• $3\,\%$ of individuals belong to group AB, and among them $82\,\%$ are rhesus positive.
A person is chosen at random in the French population.
Let:
• $A$ be the event "The person chosen has blood group A";
• $B$ be the event "The person chosen has blood group B";
• $AB$ be the event "The person chosen has blood group AB";
• $O$ be the event "The person chosen has blood group O";
• $R$ be the event "The person chosen has a positive rhesus factor".
For any event $E$, $\overline{E}$ denotes the complementary event of $E$ and $p(E)$ the probability of $E$.
1. Copy the tree, filling in the ten dotted lines. (Tree: first-level branches to $A$, $B$, $AB$, $O$, each with probability $\ldots$; from each of $A$, $B$, $AB$, branches to $R$ and $\overline{R}$ with probabilities $\ldots$; from $O$, branches to $R$ and $\overline{R}$ without dotted lines.)
2. Show that $p(B\cap R)=0.084$. Interpret this result in the context of the exercise.
3. It is given that $p(R)=0.8397$.
Show that $p_O(R)=0.83$.
4. An individual is called a "universal donor" when his blood can be transfused to any person without risk of incompatibility.
Group O with negative rhesus is the only one having this property.
Show that the probability that an individual chosen at random in the French population is a universal donor is $0.0714$.
5. During a blood drive, a sample of $100$ people is chosen in the population of a French town. This population is large enough for this choice to be treated as drawing with replacement. Let $X$ be the random variable which, to each sample of $100$ people, associates the number of universal donors in this sample.
5.a. Justify that $X$ follows a binomial distribution, and specify its parameters.
5.b. Determine, to $10^{-3}$, the probability that there are at most $7$ universal donors in this sample.
5.c. Show that the expected value $E(X)$ of the random variable $X$ is equal to $7.14$ and that its variance $V(X)$ is equal to $6.63$ to $10^{-2}$.
6. During the national blood donation week, a blood drive is organised in $N$ French towns chosen at random, numbered $1,2,3,\ldots,N$, where $N$ is a nonzero natural number.
Consider the random variable $X_1$ which, to each sample of $100$ people of town $1$, associates the number of universal donors in this sample.
The random variables $X_2$ for town $2$, $\ldots$, $X_N$ for town $N$ are defined in the same way.
It is assumed that these random variables are independent and that they have the same expected value, equal to $7.14$, and the same variance, equal to $6.63$.
Consider the random variable $M_N=\frac{X_1+X_2+\ldots+X_N}{N}$.
6.a. What does the random variable $M_N$ represent in the context of the exercise?
6.b. Compute the expected value $E(M_N)$.
6.c. Let $V(M_N)$ be the variance of the random variable $M_N$.
Show that $V(M_N)=\frac{6.63}{N}$.
6.d. Determine the smallest value of $N$ for which the Bienaymé–Chebyshev inequality makes it possible to assert that
$$P(7<M_N<7.28)\geqslant 0.95.$$

A team of biologists is studying the evolution of the area covered by a seagrass called posidonia on the floor of the bay of l'Alycastre, near the island of Porquerolles.
The zone studied has a total area of $20$ hectares (ha), and on 1 July 2024 posidonia covered $1$ ha of this zone.

Part A: study of a discrete model
For every natural number $n$, let $u_n$ be the area of the zone, in hectares, covered by posidonia on 1 July of the year $2024+n$. Thus $u_0=1$.
A study of this area established that for every natural number $n$,
$$u_{n+1}=-0.02u_n^2+1.3u_n.$$
1. Compute the area that posidonia should cover on 1 July 2025 according to this model.
2. Let $h$ be the function defined on $[0;20]$ by
$$h(x)=-0.02x^2+1.3x.$$
It is given that $h$ is increasing on $[0;20]$.
2.a. Prove that for every natural number $n$, $1\leqslant u_n\leqslant u_{n+1}\leqslant 20$.
2.b. Deduce that the sequence $(u_n)$ converges. Let $L$ be its limit.
2.c. Justify that $L=15$.
3. The biologists want to know after how long the area covered by posidonia will exceed $14$ hectares.
3.a. Without any calculation, justify that, according to this model, this will happen.
3.b. Copy and complete the following algorithm so that at the end of execution it displays the answer to the biologists' question.
$$\begin{array}{l}\texttt{def seuil():}\\ \quad\texttt{n=0}\\ \quad\texttt{u= 1}\\ \quad\texttt{while ...... :}\\ \quad\quad\texttt{n=......}\\ \quad\quad\texttt{u=......}\\ \quad\texttt{return n}\end{array}$$

Part B: study of a continuous model
We wish to describe the area of the studied zone covered by posidonia over time with a continuous model.
In this model, for a duration $t$, in years, elapsed from 1 July 2024, the area of the studied zone covered by posidonia is given by $f(t)$, where $f$ is a function defined on $[0;+\infty[$ satisfying:
• $f(0)=1$;
• $f$ does not vanish on $[0;+\infty[$;
• $f$ is differentiable on $[0;+\infty[$;
• $f$ is a solution on $[0;+\infty[$ of the differential equation

The two parts can be treated independently.
In this exercise we consider people who came to stay at a multi-sports centre over the weekend.
The requested probabilities are to be rounded to the thousandth if necessary.

Part A
The centre offers people who come for a weekend an introductory roller-skating package consisting of two lessons.
A person is chosen at random among those who have signed up for this package.
Let $A$ and $B$ be the following events:
• $A$: "The person falls during the first lesson";
• $B$: "The person falls during the second lesson".
For any event $E$, $P(E)$ denotes its probability and $\overline{E}$ its complementary event.
Observations make it possible to assume that $P(A)=0.6$.
Moreover, it is found that:
• if the person falls during the first lesson, the probability that she falls during the second is $0.3$;
• if the person does not fall during the first lesson, the probability that she falls during the second is $0.4$.
1. Represent the situation by a weighted tree.
2. Compute the probability $P\left(\overline{A}\cap B\right)$ and interpret the result.
3. Show that $P(B)=0.34$.
4. The person does not fall during the second lesson.
Compute the probability that she did not fall during the first lesson.
5. Let $X$ be the random variable which, to each sample of $100$ people who signed up for the package, associates the number of them who fell neither during the first nor during the second lesson.
The choice of a sample of $100$ people is treated as drawing with replacement.
It is given that the probability that a person falls neither during the first nor during the second lesson is $0.24$.
5.a. Show that the random variable $X$ follows a binomial distribution, and specify its parameters.
5.b. What is the probability of having, in a sample of $100$ people who signed up for the package, at least $20$ people who fall neither during the first nor during the second lesson?
5.c. Compute the expected value $E(X)$ and interpret the result in the context of the exercise.

Part B
A person who came for a weekend to the multi-sports centre is chosen at random. Let $T_1$ be the random variable giving his total waiting time, in minutes, before access to the sports activities during Saturday, and $T_2$ the random variable giving his total waiting time, in minutes, before access to the sports activities during Sunday.
It is given that:
• $T_1$ follows a probability distribution with expected value $E(T_1)=40$ and standard deviation $\sigma(T_1)=10$;
• $T_2$ follows a probability distribution with expected value $E(T_2)=60$ and standard deviation $\sigma(T_2)=16$;
• the random variables $T_1$ and $T_2$ are independent.
Let $T$ be the random variable giving the total waiting time before access to the sports activities over the two days, in minutes. Thus $T=T_1+T_2$.
1. Determine the expected value $E(T)$ of the random variable $T$. Interpret the result in the context of the exercise.
2. Show that the variance $V(T)$ of the random variable $T$ is equal to $356$.
3. Using the Bienaymé–Chebyshev inequality, show that, for a person chosen at random among those who came for a weekend to the multi-sports centre, the probability that his total waiting time $T$ lies strictly between $60$ and $140$ minutes is greater than $0.77$.
