The object of this exercise is the study of how a car on a fairground ride stops, from the moment it enters the braking zone at the end of the ride.
Let $t$ be the time elapsed, in seconds, from the moment the car arrives in the braking zone.
The distance travelled by the car in the braking zone, in metres, is modelled as a function of $t$ by a function $d$ defined on $[0;+\infty[$.
Thus $d(0)=0$.
Moreover, it is given that this function $d$ is differentiable on its domain. Let $d'$ be its derivative.

Part A
The figure (Fig. 2) shows, in an orthonormal coordinate system:
• the representative curve $\mathcal{C}_d$ of the function $d$;
• the tangent line $T$ to the curve $\mathcal{C}_d$ at the point $A$ with abscissa $4.7$;
• the asymptote $\Delta$ to $\mathcal{C}_d$ at $+\infty$.
In this part, no justification is expected.
With the precision allowed by the graph, answer the questions below.
According to this model:
1. After how long will the car have travelled $15$ m in the braking zone?
2. What minimum length must be planned for the braking zone?
3. What is the value of $d'(4.7)$? Interpret this result in the context of the exercise.

Part B
Recall that $t$ denotes the time elapsed, in seconds, from the moment the car arrives in the braking zone.
The instantaneous speed of the car, in metres per second $\left(\text{m}\cdot\text{s}^{-1}\right)$, is modelled as a function of $t$ by a function $v$ defined on $[0;+\infty[$.
It is given that:
• the function $v$ is differentiable on its domain; $v'$ denotes its derivative;
• the function $v$ is a solution of the differential equation
$$(E):\quad y'+0.6y=\mathrm{e}^{-0.6t},$$
where $y$ is an unknown function and $y'$ is the derivative of $y$.
Moreover, when it arrives in the braking zone, the speed of the car is equal to $12\ \text{m}\cdot\text{s}^{-1}$, that is, $v(0)=12$.
1.a. Consider the differential equation
$$(E'):\quad y'+0.6y=0.$$
Determine the solutions of the differential equation $(E')$ on $[0;+\infty[$.
1.b. Let $g$ be the function defined on $[0;+\infty[$ by $g(t)=t\mathrm{e}^{-0.6t}$.
Check that the function $g$ is a solution of the differential equation $(E)$.
1.c. Deduce the solutions of the differential equation $(E)$ on $[0;+\infty[$.
1.d. Deduce that for every real $t$ in the interval $[0;+\infty[$,
$$v(t)=(12+t)\mathrm{e}^{-0.6t}.$$
2. In this question, we study the function $v$ on $[0;+\infty[$.
2.a. Show that for every real $t\in[0;+\infty[$, $v'(t)=(-6.2-0.6t)\mathrm{e}^{-0.6t}$.
2.b. Assuming that
$$v(t)=12\mathrm{e}^{-0.6t}+\frac{1}{0.6}\times\frac{0.6t}{\mathrm{e}^{0.6t}},$$
determine the limit of $v$ at $+\infty$.
2.c. Study the direction of variation of the function $v$ and draw up its complete table of variations. Justify.
2.d. Show that the equation $v(t)=1$ has a unique solution $\alpha$, and give an approximate value of it to the tenth.
3. When the speed of the car is less than or equal to $1$ metre per second, a mechanical system is triggered which brings it to a complete stop.
Determine after how long this system comes into action. Justify.

Part C
Recall that for every real $t$ in the interval $[0;+\infty[$,
$$v(t)=(12+t)\mathrm{e}^{-0.6t}.$$
It is given that for every real $t$ in the interval $[0;+\infty[$,
$$d(t)=\int_0^t v(x)\,\mathrm{d}x.$$
1. Using integration by parts, show that the distance travelled by the car between the instants $0$ and $t$ is given by
$$d(t)=\mathrm{e}^{-0.6t}\left(-\frac{5}{3}t-\frac{205}{9}\right)+\frac{205}{9}.$$
2. Recall that the stopping device is triggered when the speed of the car is less than or equal to $1$ metre per second.
Determine, according to this model, an approximate value to the hundredth of the distance travelled by the car in the braking zone before this device is triggered.

El Niño is a large-scale oceanic phenomenon of the equatorial Pacific which affects wind patterns, sea temperature and precipitation over the whole globe.
In certain years, this phenomenon is said to be "dominant". Scientists seek to model the occurrence of this phenomenon.
In this exercise, Parts A and B are independent.

Part A - First model
From a sample of data, a first model is considered:
• each year, the probability that the El Niño phenomenon is dominant is equal to $0.4$;
• the occurrence of the El Niño phenomenon is independent from one year to the next.
Let $X$ be the random variable which, over a period of $10$ years, associates the number of years in which El Niño is dominant.
1. Justify that $X$ follows a binomial distribution and specify the parameters of this distribution.
2.a. Compute the probability that, over a period of $10$ years, the El Niño phenomenon is dominant in exactly $2$ years.
2.b. Compute $P(X\leqslant 2)$. What does this result mean in the context of the exercise?
3. Compute $E(X)$. Interpret this result.

Part B - Second model
After a study of a larger body of data over the last $50$ years, another model appears more relevant:
• if the El Niño phenomenon is dominant in one year, then the probability that it is dominant again the following year is $0.5$;
• on the other hand, if the El Niño phenomenon is not dominant in one year, then the probability that it is dominant the following year is $0.3$.
The reference year is $2023$.
For every natural number $n$, let:
• $E_n$ be the event "the El Niño phenomenon is dominant in the year $2023+n$";
• $p_n$ be the probability of the event $E_n$.
In $2023$, El Niño was not dominant. Thus $p_0=0$.
1. Let $n$ be a natural number. Copy and complete the following weighted tree: first branches to $E_n$ (probability $p_n$) and to $\overline{E_n}$ (probability $\ldots$); from each of $E_n$ and $\overline{E_n}$, branches to $E_{n+1}$ and $\overline{E_{n+1}}$ with probabilities $\ldots$.
2. Justify that $p_1=0.3$.
3. Using the tree, show that, for every natural number $n$,
$$p_{n+1}=0.2p_n+0.3.$$
We seek to predict the evolution of the occurrence of the El Niño phenomenon.
4.a. Conjecture the variations and the possible limit of the sequence $(p_n)$.
4.b. Show by induction that, for every natural number $n$, $p_n\leqslant\frac{3}{8}$.
4.c. Determine the direction of variation of the sequence $(p_n)$.
4.d. Deduce the convergence of the sequence $(p_n)$.
We seek to determine the limit of the sequence $(p_n)$.
5. Let $(u_n)$ be the sequence defined by $u_n=p_n-\frac{3}{8}$ for every natural number $n$.
5.a. Show that the sequence $(u_n)$ is geometric with common ratio $0.2$ and give its first term.
5.b. Show that, for every natural number $n$,
$$p_n=\frac{3}{8}\left(1-0.2^n\right).$$
5.c. Compute the limit of the sequence $(p_n)$.
5.d. Interpret this result in the context of the exercise.

The pumpkinseed sunfish is an invasive species of fish. A plan to combat the proliferation of this species has been put in place, and in this exercise two models of the evolution of the population of pumpkinseed sunfish in a natural pond are studied. It is estimated that, in this pond, the number of pumpkinseed sunfish amounted to $4000$ individuals on 1 January 2025.

Part A: study of a discrete model
In this part, the number of pumpkinseed sunfish in the pond is modelled by a sequence $(u_n)$.
For every natural number $n$, $u_n$ denotes the number of pumpkinseed sunfish, in thousands, in the pond on 1 January of the year $2025+n$.
The sequence $(u_n)$ is defined by:
• $u_0=4$;
• for every natural number $n$, $u_{n+1}=4-\frac{4}{u_n}$.
It is given that this sequence is well defined and, in particular, that for every integer $n$, $u_n>0$.
1. Compute the number of pumpkinseed sunfish on 1 January 2026 given by this model.
2. Let $h$ be the function defined on the interval $]0;+\infty[$ by $h(x)=4-\frac{4}{x}$.
2.a. Justify that the function $h$ is increasing on the interval $]0;+\infty[$.
2.b. Prove that for every natural number $n$,
$$2\leqslant u_{n+1}\leqslant u_n\leqslant 4.$$
2.c. Deduce that the sequence $(u_n)$ is convergent. Let $\ell$ be its limit.
2.d. Justify that $\ell=2$.
2.e. Does this model predict a long-term elimination of the invasive species?
3. Consider the Python script below.
$$\begin{array}{l}\texttt{def population(s) :}\\ \quad\texttt{u=4}\\ \quad\texttt{n=0}\\ \quad\texttt{while... :}\\ \quad\quad\texttt{u=...}\\ \quad\quad\texttt{n=...}\\ \quad\texttt{return n}\end{array}$$
3.a. Let $s$ be a real number in the interval $]2;4[$.
Copy and complete this script so that, after execution, it returns the smallest integer $n$ such that $u_n<s$.
3.b. What value does the command population(2.2) return?
Interpret this result in the context of the exercise.

Part B: study of a continuous model
Let $t$ be the time elapsed, in years, from 1 January 2025. The evolution of the number of pumpkinseed sunfish, in thousands, is modelled by the function $p$ such that:
• the function $p$ is defined and differentiable on the interval $[0;+\infty[$;
• $p(0)=4$;
• the function $p$ is a solution of the differential equation $(E)\ y'+y=2$, where $y$ is a function of the real variable $t$.
1. Give the set of solutions of the equation $(E)$.
2. Deduce that the expression of the function $p$ on the interval $[0;+\infty[$ is $p(t)=2\mathrm{e}^{-t}+2$.
3. Does this model predict a long-term elimination of the invasive species?

A supermarket has a stock of tomatoes coming from two suppliers $A$ and $B$.
It has been found that:
• $91\,\%$ of the stock of tomatoes is saleable;
• $60\,\%$ of the stock of tomatoes comes from supplier $A$;
• among the tomatoes coming from supplier $A$, the proportion of saleable tomatoes is $95\,\%$.
A tomato is chosen at random from the stock.
Let:
• $A$ be the event "The tomato comes from supplier $A$";
• $B$ be the event "The tomato comes from supplier $B$";
• $C$ be the event "The tomato is saleable".
For any event $E$, $P(E)$ denotes the probability of $E$.

Part A
1. Copy the tree, filling in the dotted lines: first branches to $A$ and $B$ with probabilities $\ldots$; from $A$, branches to $C$ and $\overline{C}$ with probabilities $\ldots$; from $B$, branches to $C$ and $\overline{C}$ (without dotted lines).
2.a. Determine the probability that the tomato chosen is saleable and comes from supplier $A$.
2.b. Prove that $P_B(C)=0.85$.
2.c. The tomato chosen is not saleable. The purchasing manager estimates that it is half as likely to come from supplier $A$ as from supplier $B$. Is he right?

Part B
Recall that $9\,\%$ of the tomatoes in the stock are not saleable.
1. $15$ tomatoes are taken from the stock at random and independently. The stock is considered large enough for this sampling to be treated as random drawing with replacement.
Let $X$ be the random variable equal to the number of unsaleable tomatoes in this sample of $15$ tomatoes.
1.a. It is given that the random variable $X$ follows a binomial distribution. Specify its parameters.
1.b. Determine the probability that exactly two tomatoes are unsaleable.
Give the value rounded to the thousandth.
1.c. Determine the probability that at most two tomatoes are unsaleable.
Give the value rounded to the thousandth.
2. A sample of $n$ tomatoes is now formed, still under the same conditions, where $n$ is a nonzero natural number.
Let $X_n$ be the random variable equal to the number of unsaleable tomatoes and $F_n$ the random variable equal to the frequency of unsaleable tomatoes in this sample of $n$ tomatoes.
Thus $F_n=\frac{X_n}{n}$.
It is given that the random variable $X_n$ follows the binomial distribution with parameters $n$ and $0.09$.
2.a. Compute the expected value $E(F_n)$ and express the variance $V(F_n)$ in terms of $n$.
2.b. Prove that $P(0.04<F_n<0.14)\geqslant 1-\frac{32.76}{n}$.
2.c. The purchasing manager takes a sample of $500$ tomatoes from the stock. He notices that $55$ tomatoes are not saleable.
Is this consistent with what he could expect? Justify the answer.

Part A: study of the direction of variation of a function
Consider the function $f$ defined on $\mathbb{R}$ by
$$f(x)=\frac{2x}{\sqrt{1+x^2}}.$$
1. Solve the equation $f(x)=x$.
2.a. It is given that the function $f$ is differentiable on $\mathbb{R}$.
Check that, for every real $x$, $f'(x)=\frac{2}{\left(1+x^2\right)\sqrt{1+x^2}}$.
2.b. Deduce the direction of variation of the function $f$ on $\mathbb{R}$.

Part B: study of the convergence of a recursive sequence
The sequence $(u_n)$ is defined by $u_0=1$ and, for every natural number $n$, $u_{n+1}=f(u_n)$.
1. Prove by induction that, for every natural number $n$, $1\leqslant u_n\leqslant u_{n+1}<\sqrt{3}$.
2. Deduce that the sequence $(u_n)$ converges and determine its limit.
3. The aim of this question is to recover, by another method, the results of question 2 of Part B.
For every natural number $n$, let
$$v_n=\frac{u_n^2}{3-u_n^2}.$$
It is given that the sequence $(v_n)$ is well defined.
3.a. Prove that the sequence $(v_n)$ is a geometric sequence with common ratio $4$, and give its first term.
3.b. Deduce an expression of $v_n$ in terms of $n$, then that $u_n=\sqrt{\frac{1.5\times 4^n}{1+0.5\times 4^n}}$ for every natural number $n$.
3.c. Deduce the limit of the sequence $(u_n)$.

Part C: study of the convergence of the sum of terms
For every nonzero natural number $n$, let $S_n=u_0^2+u_1^2+\ldots+u_{n-1}^2$.
1. Copy and complete the Python script below so that it lists the first $p$ terms of the sequence $(S_n)$.
$$\begin{array}{l}\texttt{from math import*}\\ \\ \texttt{def termes(p) :}\\ \quad\texttt{u = ...}\\ \quad\texttt{S=0}\\ \quad\texttt{L= [ ]}\\ \quad\texttt{for i in range(p)}\\ \quad\quad\texttt{S=...}\\ \quad\quad\texttt{u= ...}\\ \quad\quad\texttt{L.append(S)}\\ \quad\texttt{return L}\end{array}$$
Remark: recall that in Python,
• the command L= [ ] creates an empty list;
• the command L.append(S) adds the additional element S at the end of the list L.
2. Recall that, for every natural number $k$, $1\leqslant u_k\leqslant\sqrt{3}$.
Prove that, for every nonzero natural number $n$, $n\leqslant S_n\leqslant 3n$.
3. Deduce the respective limits of $S_n$ and of $\frac{S_n}{n^2}$ as $n$ tends to $+\infty$.

Consider the function $f$ defined on the interval $]0;+\infty[$ by
$$f(x)=x(\ln x)^2.$$
It is given that the function $f$ is differentiable on the interval $]0;+\infty[$. Let $f'$ be its derivative.
1. Determine the limit of the function $f$ at $+\infty$.
2. For every real $x>0$, let $g(x)=x\ln x$.
2.a. Prove that for every real $x>0$, $f(x)=4\left(g\left(\sqrt{x}\right)\right)^2$.
2.b. Deduce $\displaystyle\lim_{x\to 0}f(x)$.
3. In this question, we study the variations of the function $f$ on the interval $]0;+\infty[$.
3.a. Prove that on the interval $]0;+\infty[$, $f'(x)=(\ln x)(2+\ln x)$.
3.b. Deduce the variations of the function $f$ on the interval $]0;+\infty[$.
3.c. Give the exact value of the maximum of the function $f$ on the interval $]0;1]$.
4. Consider the equation $f(x)=2$.
4.a. Justify that, on the interval $]0;+\infty[$, this equation has a unique solution.

The international fencing federation sets manufacturing standards for the blades of fencers' weapons in order to guarantee their safety as far as possible.
To test the compliance of the steel used, the blade is bent and then straightened every second until it breaks.
The blade is compliant if it breaks after more than five hours of testing.
A fencing equipment supplier buys from three blade manufacturers.
His stock consists of $60\,\%$ of blades from supplier $A$, $12\,\%$ of blades from supplier $B$, the rest coming from supplier $C$.
A quality study showed that:
• $90\,\%$ of the blades from supplier $A$ were compliant;
• $95\,\%$ of the blades from supplier $B$ were compliant;
• $85\,\%$ of the blades from supplier $C$ were compliant.

Part A
A check is carried out on one of the blades sold by the equipment supplier.
Consider the following events:
• $A$: "The blade tested comes from supplier $A$";
• $B$: "The blade tested comes from supplier $B$";
• $C$: "The blade tested comes from supplier $C$";
• $T$: "The blade tested is compliant".
$\overline{T}$ denotes the complementary event of $T$.
1. Copy and complete the probability tree representing the situation: first-level branches to $A$, $B$, $C$ with probabilities $\ldots$; from each of $A$, $B$, $C$, branches to $T$ and $\overline{T}$ with probabilities $\ldots$.
2. Determine $P\left(A\cap\overline{T}\right)$ and interpret this result in the context of the exercise.
3. Prove that the probability that the blade tested is compliant is $0.892$.
4. Given that the blade tested is not compliant, determine the probability that it comes from supplier $B$. Give the value rounded to the thousandth.

Part B
By Part A, the probability that a blade of the equipment supplier is not compliant is equal to $0.108$.
At a fencing competition, the equipment supplier brings a sample of $75$ blades from his stock.
It is considered that he chose them at random and independently.
Moreover, his stock of blades is large enough for this choice to be treated as drawing with replacement.
Let $X$ be the random variable equal to the number of non-compliant blades in this sample.
1. It is given that the random variable $X$ follows a binomial distribution.
Specify its parameters.
2. Compute the probability that exactly $6$ blades are non-compliant in this sample. Round the result to the thousandth.
3. The equipment supplier asserts that the probability that there are strictly more than $8$ non-compliant blades in this sample is less than $50\,\%$.
Is he right?

Part C
Let $n$ be a strictly positive integer denoting the number of competitions at which the equipment supplier is present.
Each time he brings a sample of $75$ blades.
The random variables $X_1,\ldots,X_n$, which are considered independent, give for each sample the number of non-compliant blades.
Let $M_n=\frac{X_1+X_2+\cdots+X_n}{n}$.
1. Determine the expected value $E(M_n)$ and the variance $V(M_n)$ of the random variable $M_n$.
2. Justify the following inequality, for every nonzero natural number $n$:
$$P\left(\left|M_n-8.1\right|\geqslant 2\right)\leqslant\frac{1.8063}{n}.$$
3. Determine a value of the integer $n$ from which $P\left(\left|M_n-8.1\right|<2\right)\geqslant 0.95$.
Interpret this result in the context of the exercise.

Statement 5: $\displaystyle\lim_{n\to+\infty}S_n=\frac{\mathrm{e}}{\mathrm{e}-1}$.

Among the inhabitants aged at least $15$ living in France, there are:
• $21\,\%$ of people aged $15$ to $29$;
• $46\,\%$ of people aged $30$ to $59$;
• $33\,\%$ of people aged at least $60$.
We study the use of a social network by the inhabitants aged at least $15$ living in France.
It has been observed that:
• $70\,\%$ of the people aged $15$ to $29$ have already posted on this social network;
• $46\,\%$ of the people aged $30$ to $59$ have already posted on this social network;
• $15\,\%$ of the people aged at least $60$ have already posted on this social network.
A person aged at least $15$ living in France is questioned and asked whether she has already posted on this social network.
Let:
• $J$ be the event "the person questioned is between $15$ and $29$ years old";
• $M$ be the event "the person questioned is between $30$ and $59$ years old";
• $S$ be the event "the person questioned is at least $60$ years old";
• $R$ be the event "the person questioned has already posted on this social network".
$\overline{R}$ denotes the complementary event of the event $R$.
Throughout the exercise, approximate values are to be rounded to the thousandth.

Part A
1. Copy and complete the probability tree (first-level branches to $J$, $M$, $S$; from each of them, branches to $R$ and $\overline{R}$).
2. Determine $P(M\cap R)$.
Interpret the result in the context of the exercise.
3. A person aged at least $15$ living in France is questioned at random.
3.a. Compute the probability that she has already posted on this social network.
3.b. It is known that this person has already posted on this social network.
Determine the probability that she is at least $60$ years old.

Part B
In a survey, $100$ people aged at least $15$ living in France are questioned successively, at random and independently, and asked whether they have already posted on this social network.
The population of the country is large enough for the choice of the people surveyed to be treated as successive draws with replacement.
Let $X$ be the random variable giving the number of people who have already posted on this social network among these $100$ people questioned.
In this part, it is given that the probability that a person aged at least $15$ living in France has already posted on this social network is $0.41$.
1. It is given that the random variable $X$ follows a binomial distribution.

We study the operation of a heating system installed in a room.
This system switches on automatically as soon as the temperature of the room is less than or equal to $18\,^\circ$C (degrees Celsius), and switches off when it reaches $20\,^\circ$C.

Part A: Heating phase
For a room temperature varying from $18\,^\circ$C to $20\,^\circ$C, the heating system runs continuously. The temperature of the room increases progressively.
In this part, the temperature of the room, in degrees Celsius, at time $t$, expressed in tens of minutes, is modelled by a function $T$ defined on $[0;+\infty[$.
It is given that the function $T$ is:
• differentiable on $[0;+\infty[$;
• a solution of the differential equation
$$(E):\quad y'=-0.035y+0.91,$$
where $y$ is a function of the variable $t$, defined and differentiable on $[0;+\infty[$.

$$T(t)=26-8\mathrm{e}^{-0.035t}.$$

Part C
Two geographical zones are served, deliveries in one having no effect on those in the other:
• in zone $A$, delivery times are met in $85\,\%$ of cases;
• in zone $B$, delivery times are met in $90\,\%$ of cases.
The company observes $120$ deliveries made in zone $A$ and $80$ deliveries made in zone $B$.
Let:
• $X_A$ be the random variable counting the number of parcels delivered on time in zone $A$;
• $X_B$ be the random variable counting the number of parcels delivered on time in zone $B$;
• $S=X_A+X_B$ be the random variable giving the total number of parcels delivered on time.
It is given that $X_A$ follows a binomial distribution $\mathcal{B}(120;0.85)$ and that $X_B$ follows a binomial distribution $\mathcal{B}(80;0.90)$.
1. Compute the expected value and the variance of the variables $X_A$ and $X_B$.
2. Compute $E(S)$.
3. Which condition makes it possible to assert that $V(S)=22.5$?
4. Using a Bienaymé–Chebyshev inequality, find a lower bound for $P(S\in[165;183])$ and interpret the result.

Part A
Let $f$ be the function defined on $]-3;+\infty[$ by
$$f(x)=\frac{2x}{x+3}.$$
It is given that $f$ is differentiable on $]-3;+\infty[$.
1. Check, showing the calculations in detail, that for every real $x$ in $]-3;+\infty[$, $f'(x)=\frac{6}{(x+3)^2}$.
Deduce that $f$ is increasing on $]-3;+\infty[$.
Let $(u_n)$ be the sequence defined by $u_0=1$ and, for every natural number $n$, by $u_{n+1}=f(u_n)$.
2. Prove by induction that for every integer $n$, $0\leqslant u_{n+1}\leqslant u_n\leqslant 1$.
3. Deduce that $(u_n)$ is convergent.

Part A
Consider the differential equation
$$(E):\quad 2y'+3y=8\mathrm{e}^{-\frac{3}{2}t},$$
where $y$ is a function of the variable $t$, defined and differentiable on $[0;+\infty[$.
1. Solve on the interval $[0;+\infty[$ the differential equation
$$(E'):\quad 2y'+3y=0.$$
2. Let $f$ be the differentiable function on $[0;+\infty[$ defined by
$$f(t)=4t\mathrm{e}^{-\frac{3}{2}t}.$$
It is given that this function $f$ is a solution of the differential equation $(E)$.
Consider a function $g$ defined and differentiable on $[0;+\infty[$.

Part B
A clinical trial is carried out with several volunteer patients in order to validate or not the effectiveness of a medicine.
The patient is asked to swallow the medicine in the form of a $1$ mg tablet, and then the quantity of this medicine present in the blood over time is studied.
The quantity of this medicine, in mg, as a function of the time elapsed after taking the tablet, is modelled by the function $f$, differentiable on $[0;+\infty[$, defined by
$$f(t)=4t\mathrm{e}^{-\frac{3}{2}t},\quad t\ \text{being expressed in hours}.$$
1. Determine $\displaystyle\lim_{t\to+\infty}f(t)$.
Interpret this result in the context of the exercise.
2.a. Check, showing the calculations in detail, that for every positive real $t$, $f'(t)=(4-6t)\mathrm{e}^{-\frac{3}{2}t}$.
2.b. Study the sign of the derivative and deduce the table of variations of the function $f$ on $[0;+\infty[$.
2.c. After how long is the quantity of this medicine present in the blood maximal?
3. Prove that the equation $f(t)=0.5$ has a unique solution on $[1;3]$.
Give an interval of width $10^{-2}$ containing this solution, denoted $\alpha$.
4. The clinical trial will be validated if the following two conditions are satisfied:
— Condition 1: $50\,\%$ of the quantity of the medicine is eliminated from the body at the latest $2$ hours after taking the tablet.
— Condition 2: the mean quantity of the medicine present in the patient's body between $1$ hour and $3$ hours after taking the tablet is less than $0.40$ mg.
Is condition 1 satisfied?
Is condition 2 satisfied?
